title: Playgrounds
text:
Playgrounds

Learn Codly by changing a working example. Each page combines editable Typst source with controls for common options; Copy code captures your edits and the current control values, ready to paste into a document.

| Playground | Try |
| --- | --- |
| [Layout and excerpts](layout.md) | Fit long lines, compare themes, select source ranges, and add a review gutter. |
| [Annotations and references](annotations.md) | Highlight characters, attach explanations, and link to code from prose. |
| [Diffs and mixed languages](diffs-and-syntax.md) | Style a patch, tune its gutters, and highlight Python inside a shell script. |

See the [API reference](../api/index.md) for complete field definitions, or [queries and show rules](../api/queries-and-show-rules.md) for custom components.

title: Layout and excerpts
text:
Layout and excerpts

Tune a code block for the space around it, then select parts of a larger file without losing their source coordinates.

 Fit long lines

Reduce the width to compare ordinary wrapping with smart indentation; the wrap marker appears on continuation lines when smart indentation is enabled.

Row inset adds space around each line; block padding adds space around the whole block. Moving numbers outside places them beside the code border.

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: layout-theme
  label: Theme
  default: '"github-light"'
  options:
    - label: GitHub Light
      value: '"github-light"'
    - label: Dark
      value: '"dark"'
    - label: Clean
      value: '"clean"'
- type: slider
  name: layout-width
  label: Block width
  default: '100%'
  min: 55
  max: 100
  step: 5
  unit: '%'
- type: slider
  name: layout-size
  label: Code size
  default: '9pt'
  min: 7
  max: 12
  step: 1
  unit: pt
- type: slider
  name: layout-radius
  label: Corner radius
  default: '4pt'
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
  unit: pt
- type: slider
  name: layout-inset
  label: Row inset
  default: '3pt'
  min: 2
  max: 8
  step: 1
  unit: pt
- type: slider
  name: layout-padding
  label: Block padding
  default: '0pt'
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
  unit: pt
- type: switch
  name: layout-numbers
  label: Show line numbers
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: layout-outside
  label: Numbers outside the block
  default: false
- type: switch
  name: layout-smart-indent
  label: Smart indentation
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: layout-wrap-marker
  label: Show wrap marker
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.theme(layout-theme, block: (text: (size: layout-size)))
show: codly.line-set_(inset: layout-inset)
show: codly.number-set_(
  placement: if layout-outside { "outside" } else { "inside" },
)

codly.new(
  py
  def send_digest(address, updates):
      if updates:
          subject = "Your weekly project updates are ready to read"
          send_email(address, subject=subject, body=format_updates(updates))
      return {"recipient": address, "delivered": bool(updates)}
  ,
  file: "digest.py",
  width: layout-width,
  radius: layout-radius,
  padding: layout-padding,
  number-enabled: layout-numbers,
  smart-indent: layout-smart-indent,
  wrap-marker: if layout-wrap-marker { [↪] } else { none },
)


See [codly.new](../api/components/new.md) for block fields and [codly.theme](../api/helpers/theme.md) for styling individual components.

 Show an excerpt with a review gutter

The review marks belong to source lines 2, 4, and 7; they stay attached when the excerpt or numbering offset changes.

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: excerpt-ranges
  label: Source selection
  default: none
  options:
    - label: Whole file
      value: none
    - label: Function body (2–7)
      value: '((2, 7),)'
    - label: Two excerpts (2–4 and 7–8)
      value: '((2, 4), (7, 8))'
- type: slider
  name: excerpt-offset
  label: Numbering offset
  default: '0'
  min: 0
  max: 100
  step: 10
- type: switch
  name: excerpt-numbers
  label: Show line numbers
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: excerpt-review
  label: Show review gutter
  default: true
- type: slider
  name: excerpt-gutter-width
  label: Review gutter width
  default: '18pt'
  min: 12
  max: 30
  step: 2
  unit: pt
- type: switch
  name: excerpt-smart-skip
  label: Show omitted-line markers
  default: true
- type: select
  name: excerpt-fills
  label: Row backgrounds
  default: '(rgb("f6f8fa"), white)'
  options:
    - label: Alternating
      value: '(rgb("f6f8fa"), white)'
    - label: Solid
      value: 'rgb("f6f8fa")'
    - label: No fill
      value: none
- type: switch
  name: excerpt-guides
  label: Show indentation guides
  default: true
- type: select
  name: excerpt-guide-width
  label: Spaces per guide level
  default: '4'
  options:
    - label: Infer from source
      value: auto
    - label: Two spaces
      value: '2'
    - label: Four spaces
      value: '4'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.theme("github-light", block: (text: (size: 9pt)))
show: codly.line-set_(fill: excerpt-fills)

codly.new(
  py
  def visible_names(records):
      names = []
      for record in records:
          if record["active"]:
              name = record["name"].strip()
              names.append(name)
      return sorted(names)
  print(visible_names(records))
  ,
  file: "names.py",
  ranges: excerpt-ranges,
  offset: excerpt-offset,
  number-enabled: excerpt-numbers,
  smart-skip: excerpt-smart-skip,
  indent-guides: if excerpt-guides {
    (width: excerpt-guide-width)
  } else { false },
  gutters: if excerpt-review {
    (auto, codly.gutter-column(
      values: (none, "?", none, "!", none, none, "✓", none),
      width: excerpt-gutter-width,
      align: center,
      text: (fill: rgb("8250df")),
    ))
  } else { auto },
)


> [!NOTE] Source lines and displayed numbers differ.
> ranges and gutter arrays use original source lines. offset changes displayed numbers; it does not move the selected lines or review marks.

See [codly.range](../api/types/range.md), [codly.smart-skip](../api/types/smart-skip.md), and [codly.gutter-column](../api/types/gutter-column.md) for the selection and gutter rules. Continue with [annotations and references](annotations.md) to attach explanations to those lines.

title: Annotations and references
text:
Annotations and references

Mark expressions, group lines, attach notes, and link to all of them from prose.

 Highlights, annotations, and references

References follow displayed numbering: change the offset and the highlight reference moves with it, while the annotation stays attached to the same source lines.

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: highlight-palette
  label: Highlight palette
  default: '(blue, purple)'
  options:
    - label: Blue and purple
      value: '(blue, purple)'
    - label: Orange and red
      value: '(orange, red)'
    - label: Green and aqua
      value: '(green, aqua)'
- type: slider
  name: highlight-start
  label: First character (zero-based)
  default: 9
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: highlight-length
  label: Highlight length
  default: 7
  min: 1
  max: 9
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: line-offset
  label: Displayed line offset
  default: 0
  min: 0
  max: 30
  step: 1
- type: switch
  name: annotation-enabled
  label: Show the annotation
  default: true
- type: slider
  name: annotation-end
  label: Last annotated source line
  default: 3
  min: 2
  max: 4
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: highlight-radius
  label: Highlight corner radius
  default: 3pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 8
  step: 1
- type: select
  name: reference-mode
  label: Reference suffix
  default: '"line"'
  options:
    - label: Displayed line number
      value: '"line"'
    - label: Highlight tag or annotation text
      value: '"item"'
- type: select
  name: highlight-tag
  label: Highlight tag
  default: '"step"'
  options:
    - label: step
      value: '"step"'
    - label: compute
      value: '"compute"'
    - label: result
      value: '"result"'

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.highlight-set_(color: highlight-palette, radius: highlight-radius)
show: codly.ref-set_(by: reference-mode, sep: " · ")

figure(caption: [A processing pipeline])[
  codly.new(
    py
    data = load()
    result = compute(data)
    validate(result)
    return result
    ,
    offset: line-offset,
    highlights: (
      (line: 2 + line-offset, start: highlight-start,
       end: highlight-start + highlight-length,
       tag: highlight-tag, label:  ),
      (line: 4 + line-offset, start: 7, end: 13),
    ),
    annotations: if annotation-enabled {
      ((start: 2, end: annotation-end,
        content: [Processing], label:  ),)
    } else { () },
  )
] 

The selected span is @selected-span.
if annotation-enabled [The annotated range is @processing.]
The computation starts at ref(label("analysis-code:" + str(2 + line-offset))).


Highlight line values use displayed line numbers; their start and exclusive end count characters from zero. Annotation ranges use source line numbers, starting at one with an inclusive end. The labelled enclosing figure supplies the reference target automatically. Item references use a highlight's tag or an annotation's content.

See [highlight bounds](../api/types/highlight-config.md), [annotation ranges](../api/types/annotation-config.md), and [reference formatting](../api/components/ref.md).

 Pointed bubbles and plain callouts

Two pointers on one line show how bubbles share a row or move into separate lanes as their preferred width and gap change.

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: bubble-placement
  label: Bubble placement
  default: '"below"'
  options:
    - label: Below the source line
      value: '"below"'
    - label: Above the source line
      value: '"above"'
- type: slider
  name: pointer-position
  label: First pointer character
  default: 13
  min: 0
  max: 25
  step: 1
- type: select
  name: pointer-alignment
  label: Bubble alignment around pointer
  default: '"center"'
  options:
    - label: Start
      value: '"start"'
    - label: Center
      value: '"center"'
    - label: End
      value: '"end"'
- type: slider
  name: bubble-width
  label: Preferred bubble width
  default: 100pt
  unit: pt
  min: 55
  max: 145
  step: 5
- type: slider
  name: bubble-gap
  label: Gap between bubbles
  default: 5pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
- type: select
  name: bubble-style
  label: Bubble paint
  default: '(fill: aqua.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + teal)'
  options:
    - label: Aqua with teal outline
      value: '(fill: aqua.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + teal)'
    - label: Yellow with orange outline
      value: '(fill: yellow.lighten(80%), stroke: 0.6pt + orange)'
    - label: White with gray outline
      value: '(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + gray)'
- type: slider
  name: bubble-radius
  label: Bubble corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 10
  step: 1
- type: switch
  name: source-indent
  label: Follow source indentation
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: plain-callout-enabled
  label: Show the plain callout
  default: true

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.bubble-set_(
  fill: bubble-style.fill,
  stroke: bubble-style.stroke,
  width: bubble-width,
  gap: bubble-gap,
  radius: bubble-radius,
  pointer-align: pointer-alignment,
)
show: codly.callout-set_(source-indent: source-indent)

codly.new(
  py
  def invoice(subtotal, tax):
      total = subtotal + tax
      return total
  print(invoice(80, 16))
  ,
  callouts: (
    (line: 2, pointer: pointer-position, placement: bubble-placement,
     body: [The base amount before tax.]),
    (line: 2, pointer: 24, placement: bubble-placement,
     body: [Tax is added once.]),
  ) + if plain-callout-enabled {
    ((line: 3, body: [The computed total is returned.]),)
  } else { () },
)


Callout line values use source lines, unaffected by numbering offsets. A pointer counts source characters from one, with 0 anchoring the start; pointer: none makes a plain callout. Only plain callouts follow source-indent. Bubble width is a preference: Codly keeps each bubble within the available row and wraps its text.

See [callout configuration](../api/types/callout-config.md) and [bubble styles](../api/components/bubble.md). To style selected elements with show rules, continue with [queries and show rules](../api/queries-and-show-rules.md).

title: Diffs and mixed languages
text:
Diffs and mixed languages

Highlight changes in a patch, and embedded code inside another language.

 Review a Python change

This patch replaces a positional result with named fields. Old and new code get independent syntax passes, so removed delimiters or multiline strings do not disturb the highlighting of added code. The custom gutter shows patch-row coordinates and replaces the automatic old/new/marker columns.

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: patch-enabled
  label: Process the patch
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: patch-numbers
  label: Old and new numbers
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: patch-markers
  label: Added and removed markers
  default: true
- type: select
  name: patch-colors
  label: Change colors
  default: '(added: rgb("dafbe1"), removed: rgb("ffebe9"), meta: rgb("ddf4ff"))'
  options:
    - label: Green and red
      value: '(added: rgb("dafbe1"), removed: rgb("ffebe9"), meta: rgb("ddf4ff"))'
    - label: Blue and orange
      value: '(added: rgb("dbeafe"), removed: rgb("ffedd5"), meta: rgb("f1f5f9"))'
    - label: No background
      value: '(added: none, removed: none, meta: none)'
- type: slider
  name: patch-old-offset
  label: Old number offset
  default: '0'
  min: 0
  max: 100
  step: 10
- type: slider
  name: patch-new-offset
  label: New number offset
  default: '0'
  min: 0
  max: 100
  step: 10
- type: switch
  name: patch-custom-gutter
  label: Custom patch-row gutter
  default: false
- type: switch
  name: patch-rainbow
  label: Color nested delimiters
  default: true
- type: slider
  name: patch-width
  label: Block width
  default: '100%'
  min: 55
  max: 100
  step: 5
  unit: '%'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  diff-py
  @@ -20,3 +20,6 @@
   def summarize(values):
  -    totals = [sum(values), len(values)]
  -    return totals
  +    totals = {
  +        "sum": sum(values),
  +        "count": len(values),
  +    }
  +    return totals
  ,
  diff: if patch-enabled {
    (
      numbers: patch-numbers,
      markers: patch-markers,
      added-fill: patch-colors.added,
      removed-fill: patch-colors.removed,
      meta-fill: patch-colors.meta,
      old-offset: patch-old-offset,
      new-offset: patch-new-offset,
    )
  } else { false },
  gutters: if patch-custom-gutter {
    (codly.gutter-column(
      values: row => if row.source-line != none {
        "R" + str(row.source-line)
      },
      align: right,
      text: (fill: gray),
    ),)
  } else { auto },
  rainbow: patch-rainbow,
  width: patch-width,
)


Both diff-py and diff,py are valid Codly language tags. The hyphenated fence also works in Typst 0.15; on versions without comma support in fences, use raw(source, block: true, lang: "diff,py").

See [codly.diff](../api/types/diff.md) for patch coordinates and [codly.gutter-column](../api/types/gutter-column.md) for custom columns.

 Highlight Python inside a shell script

The shell launches Python through a heredoc, so lines 3–10 need Python highlighting inside a shell block. Without the sublanguage, the shell grammar treats that region as a string.

Each sublanguage has its own delimiter stack. Rainbow coloring skips delimiters in strings and comments, and indentation guides follow leading spaces.

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: embedded-enabled
  label: Highlight embedded code
  default: true
- type: select
  name: embedded-language
  label: Embedded language
  default: '"py"'
  options:
    - label: Python
      value: '"py"'
    - label: Plain text
      value: '"text"'
- type: switch
  name: syntax-rainbow
  label: Color nested delimiters
  default: true
- type: select
  name: syntax-palette
  label: Delimiter and guide palette
  default: '(rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a"))'
  options:
    - label: Red, blue, green
      value: '(rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a"))'
    - label: Purple, teal, orange
      value: '(rgb("7c3aed"), rgb("0f766e"), rgb("c2410c"))'
    - label: One blue
      value: '(rgb("005cc5"),)'
- type: slider
  name: syntax-depth-offset
  label: Starting palette index
  default: '0'
  min: 0
  max: 4
  step: 1
- type: switch
  name: syntax-guides
  label: Show indentation guides
  default: true
- type: select
  name: syntax-indent-width
  label: Spaces per guide level
  default: '4'
  options:
    - label: Infer from source
      value: auto
    - label: Two spaces
      value: '2'
    - label: Four spaces
      value: '4'
- type: switch
  name: syntax-numbers
  label: Show line numbers
  default: true
- type: slider
  name: syntax-width
  label: Block width
  default: '100%'
  min: 55
  max: 100
  step: 5
  unit: '%'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  sh
  !/usr/bin/env bash
  python3 - <<'PY'
  def summarize(values):
      stats = {
          "sum": sum(values),
          "count": len(values),
      }
      return {"stats": stats, "items": list(values)}

  print(summarize([2, 4, 8]))
  PY
  echo "Report ready"
  ,
  sublangs: if embedded-enabled {
    (codly.sublang(start: 3, end: 10, lang: embedded-language),)
  } else { () },
  rainbow: (
    enabled: syntax-rainbow,
    palette: syntax-palette,
    depth-offset: syntax-depth-offset,
  ),
  indent-guides: (
    enabled: syntax-guides,
    width: syntax-indent-width,
  ),
  number-enabled: syntax-numbers,
  width: syntax-width,
)


Sublanguage ranges count original source lines, starting at 1. If you insert lines above the Python section, update start and end in the editor.

See [codly.sublang](../api/types/sublang.md), [codly.rainbow](../api/types/rainbow.md), and [codly.indent-guides](../api/types/indent-guides.md) for the individual options, or [Internals](../api/internals.md) for the rendering pipeline.

title: Migrating from 1.3.0 / 1.3.1
text:
Migrating from 1.3.0 and 1.3.1 to 2.0

Version 2 replaces state-changing configuration calls with explicit code elements and scoped show rules. Most data structures carry over unchanged; styling moves to the component that owns it.

This guide covers both 1.3.0 and 1.3.1, whose configuration APIs are identical. Where 1.3.1 behavior differs — nested highlights, local highlight overrides, icon spacing, reference and grid fixes — the relevant section says so.

Each section shows the old code, its replacement, and an editable 2.0 example. The 1.3 snippets are for comparison only; widget controls and source edits apply to the new example, and Copy code captures both.

| If your document uses… | Start here |
| --- | --- |
| codly-init, codly(...), or local(...) | [Initialization](initialization) and [scoped settings](scoped-settings) |
| Enable/disable helpers | [Conversion boundaries](enable-and-disable) |
| inset, stroke, fill, or zebra-fill | [Geometry and typography](migration-typography-and-spacing) and [row fills](migration-row-fills) |
| languages, lang-, or lang-format | [Language definitions](migration-language-definitions) and [formatters](migration-language-formatters) |
| Headers, footers, or filename presentation | [Headers and footers](migration-headers-and-footers) and [filenames](migration-filename-badges) |
| Ranges, skips, or continued numbering | [Ranges](migration-ranges), [explicit skips](migration-explicit-skips), and [offsets](migration-offset) |
| Number formatting or hidden numbers | [Number styling and visibility](migration-numbers) |
| Highlights or annotations | [Whole-line highlights](migration-whole-line-highlights), [character spans](migration-span-highlights), and [annotations](migration-annotations) |
| References or internal queries | [References](migration-references) and [custom rules and queries](custom-rules-and-queries) |

::: collapse Update imports and initialize automatic conversion {initialization}

In 1.3, codly-init installed the raw-block show rules and figure handling. The codly function then changed configuration; it did not take a code block as its positional body.

Before — 1.3.0 or 1.3.1:

typst
import "@preview/codly:1.3.1": 
show: codly-init
codly(number-format: numbering.with("1."))


After — 2.0: import the namespace, set defaults with show rules, and register codly.new as the raw-block converter. codly.new(body, ..fields) constructs a block; the exported codly.codly is an alias of this constructor, not the old configuration function.

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: setup-numbers
  label: Show line numbers
  default: true
- type: select
  name: setup-numbering
  label: Number format
  default: '"1."'
  options:
    - label: Plain
      value: '"1"'
    - label: With a dot
      value: '"1."'
    - label: In parentheses
      value: '"(1)"'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.set_(number-enabled: setup-numbers)
show: codly.number-set_(numbering: setup-numbering)
show raw.where(block: true): codly.new

py
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
print(greet("reader"))



The selector only converts block raw content; inline raw keeps Typst's ordinary rendering. If you build every listing with an explicit codly.new(...), omit the converter rule entirely.

Codly 2.0 requires Typst 0.15 or newer. These examples import @preview/codly:2.0.0; when working from a checkout, import "codly.typ" or a locally installed "@local/codly:2.0.0" instead.

See [codly.new](api/components/new.md) for accepted bodies and fields.

:::

::: collapse Replace configuration state with scoped defaults and explicit blocks {scoped-settings}

In 1.3, codly(...) mutated state for the raw blocks that followed. local(...) applied temporary overrides, with nested: true to merge an enclosing local configuration. Block-specific settings — ranges, offsets, skips, highlights, annotations, headers, footers — were reset after each block.

Before:

typst
import "@preview/codly:1.3.1": 
show: codly-init
codly(radius: 2pt)

local(radius: 8pt, nested: true)[
  py
  special = True
  
]

py
ordinary = True



After: place show: codly.set_(...) in the scope whose blocks should inherit it. Component setters work the same way. An explicit argument on codly.new overrides that block's scoped default. Nested scopes inherit outer rules without a nested flag.

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: scope-outer-radius
  label: Outer corner radius
  default: 2pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: scope-inner-radius
  label: Inner corner radius
  default: 8pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: scope-padding
  label: First block padding
  default: 3pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 8
  step: 1
- type: switch
  name: scope-first-numbers
  label: First block numbers
  default: false


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.theme("github-light")
show: codly.set_(radius: scope-outer-radius)

{
  show: codly.set_(radius: scope-inner-radius)
  codly.new(
    py
    special = True
    ,
    padding: scope-padding,
    number-enabled: scope-first-numbers,
  )
}

codly.new(
  py
  ordinary = True
  ,
)


Scoped defaults apply to every matching element that follows in the scope; they are not consumed by the next block. Pass one-off data (ranges, skips, highlights, annotations) directly to codly.new, and keep shared defaults in show rules. Reusing a labelled highlight across blocks creates duplicate labels.

There is no codly-reset equivalent: end the scope to restore the enclosing configuration. To reset presentation inside a scope, apply a theme or explicit component defaults — but note that a theme does not clear block data such as ranges or annotations.

set codly.new(...) is not an Elembic set rule. Use show: codly.set_(...) for block defaults and the component setters (codly.line-set_, codly.lang-set_, …) for component fields.

:::

::: collapse Keep existing block behavior options {retained-block-options}

::: collapse Background fills, zebra striping, and fill callbacks {migration-row-fills}

Replace the two old background settings with one row fill. zebra-fill is removed. codly.line accepts a single paint, none, a nonempty palette, or a callback.

The order matters: entry 0 paints displayed row 0, entry 1 paints row 1. An old zebra-fill: none becomes a scalar fill:  ; an empty palette is invalid. fill: auto restores the default alternating pattern.

Displayed rows are not source lines. Palette indexing counts generated skip rows, callout rows, and header/footer rows. Headers and footers have their own backgrounds but still advance the index, so a header shifts the stripe of the first code line. | Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| index | Zero-based position among displayed rows, including generated rows. |
| kind | "code", "skip", or "callout" for callback rows. |
| source-line | One-based source line for code/callout rows; none for skips. |
| number | Displayed line number after offsets/skips; none for unnumbered/generated rows. |

Headers and footers never call this function. Whole-line highlights and enabled diff backgrounds take precedence over the row fill.

Note the changed callback contract: 1.3 accepted zero-argument lazy values such as fill: () => color, but the 2.0 fill callback is a row formatter.   label: Mark middle gaps
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: migration-gap-last
  label: Mark the trailing gap
  default: false

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  def process(records):
      load(records)
      validate(records)
      normalize(records)
      sort(records)
      save(records)
      report(records)
  process(records)
  ,
  ranges: migration-ranges,

    rest: migration-gap-middle,

See [range](api/types/range.md) and [smart-skip](api/types/smart-skip.md).

:::

::: collapse Port explicit skips without moving their insertion point {migration-explicit-skips}

Keep each existing (position, length) pair unchanged. The old codly-skip(position, length) helper appended a skip to the next block's state. In 2.0, supply that record in skips, optionally using codly.skip(position, length).

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly-skip(2, 8)
// Or: codly(skips: ((2, 8),))


typst code
// 2.0, inside codly.new(...):
skips: (codly.skip(2, 8),)
// Equivalent: skips: ((2, 8),)


The insertion point is the source line before which the gap row appears: position 2 puts the skip before source line 2, in both 1.3 and 2.0. Older descriptions of these positions as zero-indexed did not match the renderer — keep your working positions unchanged.

An explicit skip represents lines already absent from the source. Its length shifts subsequent displayed numbers but removes nothing: three source lines with skips: ((2, 8),) display as 1, a skip marker, 10, 11. To hide lines that are still in the source, use range/ranges with smart-skip instead.

skip-line and skip-number still set the code and number cells of the gap row, and existing content values port directly. In 2.0, an array supplies different content for successive explicit skips; automatic gaps use the fallback marker. Keep the number column enabled to see skip-number.

  default: '2'
  min: 1
  max: 3
  step: 1
- type: slider
  name: migration-skip-length
  label: Omitted line count
  default: '8'
  min: 1
  max: 20
  step: 1
- type: switch

  label: Explain the gap in its row

codly.new(
  py
  prepare()
  process()
  finish()

  skips: (codly.skip(migration-skip-position, migration-skip-length),),
  skip-line: if migration-skip-custom {
    align(center)[… migration-skip-length omitted lines …]
  } else { [⋯] },
  skip-number: [⋯],
)


See [skip](api/types/skip.md).

:::

::: collapse Replace offset-from with the unified offset field {migration-offset}

offset now takes a number, auto, or a label. The numeric form keeps its old meaning: add that number to the displayed line numbers. codly-offset(offset: 20) becomes a field on codly.new(...) or a scoped show: codly.set_(offset: 20).

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(offset: 20)
// Continue another block:
codly(offset-from:  )
// Continue it with an additional shift:
codly(offset-from:  , offset: 3)


typst code
// 2.0, inside codly.new(...):
offset: 20
offset:  
// Or start the first selected source line at 1:
offset: auto


For continuation, label the previous block (or its enclosing figure): offset:   continues from that block's last displayed number, accounting for its own offsets, selections, explicit skips, and unnumbered lines. Because the offset is relative to the predecessor, an excerpt beginning at source line 2 starts two above the predecessor's last number; to continue seamlessly, subtract first-source-line - 1 from codly.info( ).last-number in context. An empty predecessor contributes zero. Never make two blocks continue each other.

If the old document combines offset-from with an additional numeric shift, resolve that number explicitly in context:

typst
context {
  let info = codly.info( )
  let last = if info.last-number == none { 0 } else { info.last-number }
  codly.new(
    
    next line
    ,
    offset: last + 3,
  )
}


offset: auto starts an excerpt at 1. It anchors to the first selected source line that exists and keeps the gaps between disjoint intervals — it does not compress separate excerpts into a consecutive sequence.

Offsets affect displayed numbers, line-reference labels, and highlight line coordinates. Source-indexed constructs — ranges, annotation intervals, callouts, gutter arrays — keep their source coordinates. A scoped offset now applies to every matching block in the scope; it is no longer a next-block value that resets after rendering.

- type: select

  label: Second block numbering
  default: ' '

    - label: Preserve source numbers

    - label: Start the excerpt at one

  validate()
  process()
  finish()
  ,
  range: if migration-offset-excerpt { (2, 3) } else { none },
  offset: migration-offset-mode,
)


See [codly.new](api/components/new.md) and [codly.info](api/helpers/info.md).

:::

::: collapse Separate number styling from number visibility {migration-numbers}

Move number formatting onto codly.number; use number-enabled to hide the column. In 1.3, number-format: none disabled line numbers. In 2.0, codly.number's numbering accepts a native numbering pattern or callback, while the block's number-enabled field controls whether Codly generates its automatic number gutter.

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(
  number-format: numbering.with("I."),
  number-align: right + horizon,
  number-placement: "outside",
)
// To hide numbers: codly(number-format: none)


typst code
// 2.0:
show: codly.number-set_(
  numbering: "I.",
  align: right + horizon,
  placement: "outside",
)
// For one block: codly.new(..., number-enabled: false)


Callbacks still receive the numeric value, so (n) => [Ln] ports directly as numbering: (n) => [Ln]. Do not confuse this with number-show_, whose callback receives the generated element — read its integer with codly.e.fields(it).number. Use a set rule for formatting and a show rule to replace the rendered number element.

placement still accepts "inside" and "outside"; outside placement moves custom gutter columns along with the automatic number column. number-enabled: false removes only the automatic column — independent custom gutters remain.

Leaving individual lines unnumbered is new in 2.0, not a renamed 1.3 argument. unnumbered: (2,) skips numbering for source line 2 while keeping subsequent numbers contiguous; codly.unnumbered-line(2, [→]) supplies custom content for that cell. Unnumbered lines use the special reference labels covered in [references](migration-references).

:::

::: collapse Rename whole-line highlights and preserve their colors {migration-whole-line-highlights}

Rename highlighted-lines to highlighted. Existing integer entries and (line, paint) pairs still work through casts to codly.highlighted-line. These are different from the character spans in highlights, whose field name is unchanged.

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(
  highlighted-lines: (2, (4, green.lighten(80%))),
  highlighted-default-color: yellow.lighten(80%),
)


typst code
// 2.0:
show: codly.highlight-set_(color: yellow, fill: color => color.lighten(80%))
// Inside codly.new(...):
highlighted: (2, (4, green.lighten(80%)))
// Equivalent explicit entries:
highlighted: (
  codly.highlighted-line(2),
  codly.highlighted-line(4, green.lighten(80%)),
)


highlighted-default-color becomes the color and fill settings of codly.highlight: color chooses the base paint and the fill callback derives the row background from it. To keep an already-computed paint exactly, pass it in each highlighted-line entry, or use fill: color => color with that paint as color.

The line coordinate is the displayed number, in both 1.3 and 2.0. If an offset shows source line 2 as number 12, target 12. Explicit skips and unnumbered lines shift the mapping, and a source line with no displayed number cannot be targeted by highlighted at all — use row styling or a custom gutter there.

A palette array cycles through entries that lack an explicit paint; explicit paints do not advance the cycle. Whole-line and span highlights have separate cycles per block but share the configured palette. 1.3 kept highlighted-default-color (rows) and default-color (spans) independent — to preserve different colors, pin row paints explicitly in highlighted and set span defaults with highlight-set_.

See [highlighted-line](api/types/highlighted-line.md) and [highlight](api/components/highlight.md).

:::

::: collapse Port character highlights, including 1.3.1 local overrides {migration-span-highlights}

Keep highlights and its dictionaries; move shared styling onto codly.highlight. Character coordinates still start at zero, and end remains exclusive. Omitted or none start means the beginning of the line; omitted or none end means its end. The line coordinate uses displayed numbering, including offsets and explicit skips, in both versions.

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(
  highlight-radius: 3pt,
  highlight-inset: 1pt,
  highlight-fill: color => color.lighten(80%),
  highlights: ((line: 2, start: 11, end: 14, fill: orange),),
)


typst code
// 2.0:
show: codly.highlight-set_(
  radius: 3pt,
  inset: 1pt,
  fill: color => color.lighten(80%),
)
// Inside codly.new(...):
highlights: (codly.highlight-config(2, start: 11, end: 14, fill: orange),)


highlight-stroke, highlight-outset, and highlight-clip move the same way: drop the prefix and pass them to highlight-set_. Note the two roles of fill: a span entry's fill picks its base paint, while the component's fill callback transforms that paint into the box background.

1.3.1's local overrides carry over. Per-highlight inset, baseline, outset, clip, and radius — and the nested-highlight fixes — still override component defaults in 2.0, which additionally allows per-span stroke and a depth field to control stacking order. On 1.3.0 these local overrides did not work; port the shared settings first, then add exceptions.

One default changed: baseline used to derive from the bottom highlight inset; it now defaults to 0pt (auto follows the content baseline). Set it explicitly if you relied on the old positioning. Bounds must stay nonnegative and end must follow start.

    ..if migration-span-nested {

See [highlight-config](api/types/highlight-config.md) and [highlight](api/components/highlight.md).

:::

::: collapse Port annotation ranges and their numbering {migration-annotations}

Keep the source-line ranges and attach numbering to the annotation configuration. annotations remains an array of dictionaries with start, optional end, optional content, and optional label. Dictionaries cast to codly.annotation-config, so you can port them before adopting the explicit constructor.

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(
  annotation-format: numbering.with("(a)"),
  annotations: ((start: 2, end: 4, content: [body]),),
)


typst code
// 2.0, inside codly.new(...):
annotations: ((
  start: 2, end: 4, content: [body],
  numbering: numbering.with("(a)"),
),)
// Or: codly.annotation-config(2, end: 4, content: [body],
//   numbering: numbering.with("(a)"))


The global annotation-format field is gone; set numbering on each annotation, repeating the same callback for a shared format. numbering: none hides the number but keeps the content and brace. end: none still means a one-line annotation, not “through the end”.

Both endpoints are one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive; offsets change displayed numbers without moving the brace. Ranges must be positive, ordered, and non-overlapping. When selecting excerpts, include the annotation's starting line — an annotation that starts outside the excerpt is dropped, not re-anchored at the excerpt boundary.

content is ordinary Typst content; rotated labels still work. 2.0 sizes braces from the measured rows, including wrapped code, so re-check the output after changing width or pagination. A labelled annotation still needs a labelled enclosing figure, as shown in [references](migration-references).

To replace the brace entirely, use annotation-show_: read body, height, num, numbering, and the hidden label content with codly.e.fields(it), and keep that resolved label content in your replacement so references keep their anchor.

  label: First source line
  default: '2'

  step: 1

  label: Last source line
  default: '4'
  min: 3
  max: 4
  step: 1
- type: switch
  name: migration-annotation-number
  label: Show the annotation number
  default: true
- type: switch
  name: migration-annotation-rotate
  label: Rotate its text
  default: true

codly.new(
  py
  def process():
      load()
      compute()
      save()
  process()
  ,
  annotations: ((
    start: migration-annotation-start,
    end: migration-annotation-end,
    content: if migration-annotation-rotate {
      rotate(-90deg, reflow: true)[body]
    } else { [body] },
    numbering: if migration-annotation-number {
      numbering.with("(a)")
    } else { none },
  ),),
)


See [annotation-config](api/types/annotation-config.md) and [annotation](api/components/annotation.md).

:::

::: collapse Keep native references and move their formatting rules {migration-references}

Your existing @block:2, @highlight-label, and @annotation-label references can stay. Keep a label on the enclosing figure; codly.new discovers it automatically, so you do not need to repeat it as block-label. Item labels still belong on their highlight or annotation configuration.

typst code
// 1.3.0 / 1.3.1:
codly(
  reference-by: "item",
  reference-sep: " — ",
  reference-number-format: numbering.with("I"),
)


typst code
// 2.0:
show: codly.ref-set_(
  by: "item",
  sep: " — ",
  numbering: numbering.with("I"),
)


Line labels are built from the displayed integer, before the visual numbering pattern: a block with Roman numbering still uses @block:2, not @block:II. If an offset shows source line 2 as number 12, the label becomes @block:12 — keep references and highlight coordinates consistent with that mapping.

by: "line" refers to highlights and annotations by displayed line; by: "item" uses a highlight's tag, which must exist. Annotation item references changed: they now use the annotation's content instead of its formatted number. If you relied on a suffix like (a), switch to displayed-line references or override the generated codly.annotation-ref:

typst code
show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => {
  let fields = codly.e.fields(it)
  [ref(fields.block) — (a)]
})


Hiding the annotation number does not hide its item content.

For unnumbered source lines, use labels such as @block:l2p1: l2 is the preceding displayed number and p1 counts consecutive unnumbered lines after it. Numbered lines keep the normal @block:2 form.

Each reference kind is now its own generated element — codly.line-ref, codly.highlight-ref, and codly.annotation-ref — with

title: API reference
text:
API reference

- [Components](components/index.md) render code blocks and their parts.
- [Types](types/index.md) describe configuration values and their accepted shorthand forms.
- [Themes and helpers](helpers/index.md) apply reusable styles and inspect block metadata.
- [⚙️ Queries and show rules](queries-and-show-rules.md) explains how to inspect and customize elements.
- [⚙️ Internals](internals.md) follows a code block from source to layout and references.

 Imports

Import the Codly package as a namespace:

typst
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly


 Components and styling

> [!TIP] Style components with show rules.
> Use show: codly.number-set_(...) to set defaults in scope.
> The -show_ helpers accept replacement content or a callback receiving
> the component, rather than a dictionary of field overrides.

Codly uses Elembic custom elements and types; the exported codly.e gives you the same Elembic version without a separate import. [codly.new](components/new.md) creates a code block, and component helpers such as [codly.number-set_](components/number.mdsignature) apply scoped defaults with show: rather than native set syntax. See the [Elembic documentation](https://pgbiel.github.io/elembic/) for details.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.number-set_(numbering: "1.")
show raw.where(block: true): codly.new
py
print(42)
print(43)



Each component page documents its constructor and its -set_ and -show_ helpers. Configuration types do not render directly — Codly instantiates them internally — and most accept dictionaries or arrays in place of an explicit constructor call; each type page lists its accepted forms.

 Coordinates and defaults

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Source-line ranges are one-indexed and inclusive. Character highlights
> use zero-indexed offsets with an exclusive end. Displayed line numbers
> can change with offsets and skipped lines.

Callout pointers and explicit skip positions have their own conventions, documented on their type pages. Check a field's definition before using displayed numbers as configuration coordinates.

auto and none have field-specific meanings. A default value does not always describe the final appearance: themes, scoped styling rules, and surrounding Typst text or raw settings can affect rendering.

paint means a color, gradient, or tiling; array  an array of T values.

> [!WARNING] Signatures describe types.
> Signature blocks show the accepted argument types; they are not runnable
> Typst examples. Use the preview examples as a starting point for your code.

title: new
text:
codly.new

Creates a formatted code block. [codly.new](signature) is an alias of [codly.codly](signature); [codly.set_](behavior), [codly.show_](behavior), and [codly.selector](behavior) target the same element.

 Signature

typst code
codly.new(body, ..fields)


body is positional and required. It accepts source text, a path, or content containing raw blocks. Other fields are named. The setters accept named field values; show_ installs a scoped replacement callback, and selector creates a Typst selector for block instances.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | none \| str \| path \| content | Required | Raw source text, a caller-resolved file path, or content. |
| file | auto \| none \| str \| path \| content | auto | Filename badge; auto uses the input path basename and none hides it. |
| lang | auto \| none \| str | auto | Language for source or path input; auto infers from the file extension. |
| lang-position | auto \| none \| alignment | auto | Language badge placement. Top/bottom place it in header/footer; left/right alone reserves space by the first code row. |
| file-position | none \| alignment | top + left | Filename badge placement; none hides it. |
| block-label | auto \| none \| label | auto | auto uses the nearest enclosing figure's label; an unlabeled inner figure stops discovery. none disables block references; a label sets the target explicitly. |
| alias | none \| str | none | Marks a block as already aliased. |
| number-enabled | none \| bool | true | Whether the automatic line-number column is shown. |
| diff | auto \| none \| bool \| diff | auto | Diff processing; false or none disables it, while true or a diff configuration enables it. |
| gutters | auto \| array  | auto | Ordered columns before code. auto keeps the ordinary number column; an empty array hides all gutters. |
| offset | int \| label \| auto | 0 | Added to source line numbers; a label continues numbering and auto renumbers the first selected line to 1. |
| range | none \| range | none | Source-line range to display. |
| ranges | none \| array  | none | Multiple source-line ranges to display. |
| smart-skip | none \| bool \| smart-skip | false | Controls collapsed skipped lines. |
| aliases | none \| dictionary | (:) | Language aliases. |
| smart-indent | none \| bool | true | Enables indentation-aware wrapping. |
| wrap-marker | none \| content | none | Symbol shown on wrapped continuation lines when smart indentation is enabled. |
| skip-last-empty | none \| bool | true | Whether to omit a final empty source line. |
| breakable | none \| bool | true | Whether the block can break across pages. |
| skips | none \| array  | none | Explicit skipped-line configuration. |
| skip-line | none \| content \| array  | align(center)[ ... ] | Content used for skipped source lines. |
| skip-number | none \| content \| array  | [ ... ] | Content used for skipped line numbers. |
| unnumbered | none \| array  | () | Source lines to display without a line number. |
| annotations | none \| array  | none | Annotations beside source-line ranges. |
| callouts | none \| array  | none | Callouts attached to source positions. |
| highlighted | none \| array  | () | Whole-line highlights. |
| highlights | none \| array  | none | Highlight regions and palettes. |
| header | none \| content | none | Content above the code. |
| footer | none \| content | none | Content below the code. |
| radius | none \| length | 0.32em | Corner radius of the block. |
| padding | length \| dictionary | 0pt | Extra inner edge space, separate from row inset and leading. A dictionary may use top, right, bottom, left, x, y, and rest. |
| leading | none \| length | none | Vertical space between rows. |
| gutter | none \| length | none | General spacing between grid rows and columns. |
| column-gutter | none \| length | none | Horizontal spacing between block columns. |
| row-gutter | none \| length | none | Vertical spacing between block rows. |
| sublangs | none \| array  | none | Languages applied to inclusive source-line ranges. |
| rainbow | none \| bool \| rainbow | none | Opt-in syntax-aware delimiter colors. |
| indent-guides | none \| bool \| indent-guides | none | Opt-in indentation guides. |
| width | length \| ratio \| auto | 100% | Block width; auto fits natural width up to the available width. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Figure labels are discovered automatically.
> Label the enclosing figure once. Codly discovers that label automatically,
> so omit the block-label argument from codly.new.

> [!WARNING] Unlabeled inner figures stop discovery.
> A code block inside an unlabeled nested figure does not inherit an outer
> figure's label. Label the inner figure to enable references to its code.

> [!WARNING] Sublanguages cost performance.
> Each sublang block requires re-parsing and introspection; heavy use slows compilation.

Fields are validated and cast by their declared types. Gutter arrays and functions cast to gutter-column; gutters: auto includes the ordinary number column when enabled, and custom columns remain when number-enabled is false. Custom gutters replace diff's automatic old/new/marker columns. Diff colors may be paints, none, auto (the ordinary row fill), or callbacks receiving a row with diff information. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff backgrounds.

Ranges select source lines before display. Diff references count displayed patch rows; highlight and callout character positions count code characters without diff markers. Diff context uses new-side syntax, and each hunk or file is highlighted independently.

show: codly.set_(..fields) sets named field defaults in scope. show: codly.show_(it => content) replaces matching blocks with the callback result; return it inside the result to retain the block. show codly.selector(): it => content uses a native Typst selector. selector accepts outline, outer, and meta boolean options, all defaulting to false; these select Elembic representation layers rather than filtering fields.

title: lang
text:
codly.lang

Creates the language badge used by a Codly code block, with language definitions and badge styling.

 Signature

typst code
// Define a language badge for a Codly code block.
codly.lang(
  body: str,
  languages: dictionary | none = (:),
  default-color: paint | none = rgb("283593"),
  inset: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em,
  outset: dictionary | none = (x: 0.32em, y: 0em),
  radius: length | dictionary | none = 0.32em,
  stroke: stroke | function | none = (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt,
  fill: paint | function | none = (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%),
  display-name: bool | none = true,
  display-icon: bool | none = true,
  align: alignment | none = right + horizon,
)

// Equivalent set-rule for a language badge.
codly.lang-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for a language badge.
codly.lang-show_(it, ..args)


body is the required positional language key (for example, "py"). All other fields are named. [codly.lang-set_(..args)](signature) sets defaults for language badges in its scope; [codly.lang-show_(it => ...)](signature) installs a show rule that receives each badge element and returns replacement content. These helpers use the same field names as the element.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | str | Required, positional | Language key matched against languages. |
| languages | dictionary \| none | (:) | Map from language keys to definitions; see [codly.language](../types/language.md). |
| default-color | paint \| none | rgb("283593") | Color used when the matching definition has no color. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Inner padding around the badge contents. |
| outset | dictionary \| none | (x: 0.32em, y: 0em) | Placement offset used with the badge. |
| radius | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius of the badge. |
| stroke | stroke \| function \| none | (lang) => lang.color + 0.5pt | Badge border; a function receives (name: ..., icon: ..., color: ...). |
| fill | paint \| function \| none | (lang) => lang.color.lighten(80%) | Badge background; a function receives (name: ..., icon: ..., color: ...). |
| display-name | bool \| none | true | Whether to show the configured name, or the raw key when no definition exists. |
| display-icon | bool \| none | true | Whether to show the configured icon. |
| align | alignment \| none | right + horizon | Alignment used when Codly places the badge. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Unknown language keys stay visible.
> If languages has no matching entry, the badge shows the raw language key
> and uses default-color. Add a definition when you want a display name or
> icon.

The languages dictionary maps raw language tags to [codly.language](../types/language.md) values. Its values also accept a string as shorthand for a displayed name, or a dictionary. A missing entry displays the raw key and uses default-color; a matching entry supplies its name, optional icon, and optional color.

Language definitions can preserve extra fields. For a matching key, display-name, display-icon, fill, stroke, inset, and radius in that definition override the corresponding badge fields. The definition's color is used by fill and stroke callbacks through their lang dictionary; outset, align, and default-color are not per-language overrides.

If both name and icon are hidden or unavailable, the badge renders no content. Setting fill or stroke to none removes that decoration.

 Example: Typical Usage

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: badge-radius
  label: Badge radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.lang-set_(
  radius: badge-radius,
  languages: (
    py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("3476a8"), icon: "🐍"),
  ),
)

codly.lang(
  "py",
  inset: 5pt,
)


 Example: Custom Renderer

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.lang-set_(languages: (
  py: (name: [Python], color: rgb("3476a8"), icon: "🐍"),
))

show: codly.lang-show_(it => {
  // Get the fields through elembic
  let fields = codly.e.fields(it)

  // Get the language definition
  let lang = fields.languages.at(fields.body, default: none)
  if lang == none {
    return none
  }

  // Make a custom badge
  box(
    fill: lang.color.lighten(80%),
    stroke: 1pt + lang.color,
    outset: 0pt,
    inset: 2pt,
    [ lang.name - lang.icon ],
  )
})

codly.new(py
def main():
    print("Hello, Python!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
)

text:
codly.file

Creates the filename badge used beside a code block or in its header or footer.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a filename badge
codly.file(
  body: str | content,
  fill: paint | none = luma(240),
  stroke: stroke | none = 0.5pt + luma(160),
  inset: length | dictionary = (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em),
  radius: length | dictionary = 2pt,
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.file
codly.file-set_(..args)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.file
codly.file-show_(it => ...)


body is required and may be supplied positionally; it is the displayed filename or filename content. The remaining fields are named. [codly.new](new.md) documents how code blocks derive and place this badge.

[codly.file-set_(..args)](signature) sets badge defaults in scope; [codly.file-show_(it => ...)](signature) replaces each rendered badge with the callback's result.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | str \| content | Required, positional | Displayed filename. |
| fill | paint \| none | luma(240) | Badge background; none removes the fill. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 0.5pt + luma(160) | Badge border; none removes the border. |
| inset | length \| dictionary | (x: 0.4em, y: 0.2em) | Inner padding around the filename. A length applies uniformly; a dictionary can set axes independently. |
| radius | length \| dictionary | 2pt | Corner radius. A length applies uniformly; a dictionary can set corners individually. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Pass a path to codly.new
> When the code input is a path, [codly.new](new.md) reads the file, derives the badge text from its basename, and uses its extension as the language when lang is omitted. Set file or lang explicitly to override those defaults.

The badge is a box using fill, stroke, inset, and radius around body; inset and radius accept either one length or a dictionary.

title: header
text:
codly.header

Creates a configurable header element for a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a header element
codly.header(
  body,
  repeat: false,
  align: center + horizon,
  inset: auto,
  fill: luma(240),
  stroke: auto
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.header
codly.header-set_(..fields)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.header
codly.header-show_(it => ...)


body is required and positional; all other fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Content displayed in the header. |
| repeat | bool \| none | false | Repeat the header on later pages when the block breaks across pages. |
| align | alignment \| none | center + horizon | Alignment of the header content in its cell. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Space around the header content; auto leaves the grid-cell default in effect. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | luma(240) | Header cell background. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the default header fill. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke around the header cell; auto leaves the grid-cell default in effect. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Put the filename badge in the header
> codly.new places its file badge in the header by default. Supplying a custom header body keeps the badge alongside that body; style the badge separately with [codly.file-set_(...)](file.md).

When used by [codly.new](new.md), the header cell spans the code block's columns. repeat controls the underlying grid header's repetition. Setting fill to auto resolves to luma(240); the header fill is independent of line and number fills. The block's outer corner radius is configured on [codly.new](new.md), not on the header element.

[codly.header-set_(..fields)](signature) sets defaults for headers in scope; [codly.header-show_(replacement)](signature) installs a scoped replacement, whose callback receives the header element as it.

 Example

- type: select

    - label: Pale green
      value: 'rgb("d9f5df")'
    - label: No fill
      value: 'none'
- type: slider
  name: example-radius
  label: Block corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1

title: footer
text:
codly.footer

Creates the footer element rendered below a [code block](new.md).

 Signature

typst code
// Create a footer element
codly.footer(
  body,
  repeat: false,
  align: center + horizon,
  inset: auto,
  fill: none,
  stroke: auto
)

// Equivalent set-rule for codly.footer
codly.footer-set_(..args)

// Equivalent show rule for codly.footer
codly.footer-show_(it => ...)


body is required and positional; all other fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Footer content. |
| repeat | bool \| none | false | Repeat the footer on each page when the code block spans pages. |
| align | alignment \| none | center + horizon | Alignment of the footer content in its cell. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Inset around the footer content. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | none | Footer cell background. none leaves it unfilled; auto uses the footer's default. This fill is independent of line and number fills. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke around the footer cell. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Footer fill defaults to none
> fill: auto resolves to the footer's default (none). Set an explicit fill when the footer should have a background; its fill is independent of line and number fills.

Pass this element as the footer field of [codly.new](new.md); plain content is also accepted there and wrapped with the defaults. A [codly.footer-set_(...)](signature) rule supplies defaults, while fields set on an explicit [codly.footer(...)](signature) take precedence. repeat controls whether the footer appears on continuation pages.

[codly.footer-show_(callback)](signature) applies a show rule to footer elements; the callback receives the element and returns replacement content. For example, show: codly.footer-show_(it => [it]) preserves the footer body.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: footer-fill
  label: Footer fill
  default: luma(240)
  options:
    - label: Light gray
      value: 'luma(240)'
    - label: Pale blue
      value: 'rgb("e8f0ff")'
    - label: None
      value: 'none'

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  js
  const ready = true;
  ,
  footer: codly.footer([Generated output], fill: footer-fill, inset: 5pt),
)

title: line
text:
codly.line

A generated row component that styles one displayed line in a Codly code block. Codly creates these rows while rendering [codly.new](new.md); use the set/show wrappers here to configure their style.

 Signature

typst code
codly.line(body, ..fields)


body is required and positional. All other fields are named and optional.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required | Content displayed in the row. |
| radius | length \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius for the row styling. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Row padding; a dictionary accepts directional inset values. |
| fill | auto \| paint \| array  \| function \| none | (luma(240), none) | Row background. A paint or none applies to every body row; an array cycles by displayed-row index; a function receives the row dictionary described below. auto restores the default palette. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 1pt + luma(240) | Border around the row. |
| highlights | array  \| none | none | Character-level highlights for this row; see [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md). |
| smart-indent | bool | true | Continue wrapped rows at their original indentation. |
| block-label | label \| none | none | Label of the containing code block. |
| reference | dictionary \| none | none | Internal reference details for an unnumbered source line. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Whole-line highlights win.
> A row's highlight fill takes precedence over the fill selected by this
> element, so use highlight styling when a highlighted line needs a distinct
> background.

The fill callback receives a dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. index is zero-based in displayed-row order, including header, footer, skip, and callout rows — header and footer rows count toward it but do not invoke the callback. kind is "code", "skip", or "callout" for callback rows. source-line is the one-based source line for code and callout rows, and none for generated skip rows. number is the displayed line number, or none for unnumbered and generated rows.

[codly.line-set_(..args)](signature) sets row fields with show:; [codly.line-show_(it => ...)](signature) replaces or wraps each generated row, receiving the row element as it.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: row-green
  label: Code-row green channel
  default: 224
  min: 0
  max: 255
  step: 1


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.line-set_(fill: row => {
  if row.kind == "callout" { purple.lighten(80%) }
  else if row.kind == "code" { rgb(255, row-green, 190) }
  else { luma(238) }
})

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  print(answer)
  ,
  callouts: ((line: 1, body: [The value is set here.]),),
)

title: number
text:
codly.number

A displayed line number in a Codly code block; number-set_ configures its style and number-show_ replaces its rendered content.

 Signature

typst code
codly.number(number, parent, ..fields)


number and parent are required positional fields; the remaining fields are named. Codly normally creates these elements while rendering [codly.new](new.md).

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| number | none \| content \| int \| array  | Required | Value to display; none suppresses it. |
| parent | any | Required | Parent content of the line. |
| numbering | str \| function | numbering.with("1") | Numbering pattern or callback used for integer values. |
| align | alignment \| none | left + horizon | Alignment of the number in its cell. |
| placement | "inside" \| "outside" \| none | "inside" | Whether the number column sits inside or outside the code block. |
| fill | auto \| paint \| none | auto | Number-cell background; auto follows the corresponding code row's fill. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Custom content bypasses numbering.
> A content value is rendered as-is, while integer values go through
> numbering. Use an integer when you want the configured numbering style to
> apply.

An integer is formatted with numbering; an array passes its values to the numbering function as separate arguments. A content value renders as-is, and number: none displays nothing. number-set_(..fields) sets scoped fields with show:; number-show_(it => ...) replaces the generated number element with the callback's result.

The placement setting applies to the number column for code blocks in scope. Outside placement also positions any configured gutters outside the code.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: number-outside
  label: Place numbers outside
  default: false


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.number-set_(placement: if number-outside { "outside" } else { "inside" })

codly.new(
  txt
  first line
  second line
  ,
)

title: highlight
text:
codly.highlight

[codly.highlight](signature) renders a styled span over part of a source line in a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlight(body, highlight: highlight-config | none = none)
codly.highlight-set_(..args)
codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args)


 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Highlighted span content. |
| highlight | highlight-config \| none | none | Span metadata supplied by Codly, including source positions and local overrides; see [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md). |
| color | paint \| array  | Thesis theme's five-color highlight palette | Base paint or cycling palette for highlights. The palette must not be empty. |
| radius | length \| none | 0.32em | Corner radius of the highlight box. |
| fill | function \| none | color => color.lighten(80%) | Transforms the selected highlight paint into the box fill. |
| baseline | length \| auto \| none | 0pt | Baseline shift for the highlight box; auto follows the content baseline. |
| stroke | stroke \| function \| none | color => 0.5pt + color | Box stroke, or a callback that derives it from the selected paint. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0.32em | Space between the highlighted content and box edges. A dictionary uses Typst inset sides. |
| outset | length \| dictionary \| none | 0em | Space the highlight box extends outside its layout bounds. |
| clip | bool \| none | true | Whether the highlight box clips its content. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] References need a labelled figure.
> A highlight label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically.

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Highlight line numbers are one-indexed. Character offsets are zero-indexed,
> and end is exclusive.

> [!WARNING]
> A highlight palette must contain at least one color. An empty array causes
> a compilation error.

Codly emits this element for spans declared in a code block's highlights field. Span positions are zero-indexed character offsets, with an exclusive end; line numbers are one-indexed. Bounds must be nonnegative; omitted or none bounds start at the beginning or extend through the end of the line. See [codly.highlight-config](../types/highlight-config.md) for span metadata fields.

Each code block has an independent highlight-paint cycle, separate from whole-line highlighting. A scalar color repeats for every span; an array cycles in declaration order. An explicit paint in the span metadata uses that paint without advancing the cycle, while its callback receives the next palette paint. The element's fill and stroke callbacks receive that resolved span paint. Per-span radius, clip, inset, outset, baseline, and stroke settings override the corresponding element fields when present.

[codly.highlight-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields for matching highlight elements in scope; [codly.highlight-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the highlight element.

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: example-radius
  label: Corner radius
  default: 4pt
  unit: pt
  min: 0
  max: 12
  step: 1

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.highlight-set_(radius: example-radius)

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  ,
  highlights: ((line: 1, start: 4, end: 10),),
)

title: annotation
text:
codly.annotation

[codly.annotation](signature) is the generated brace element displayed beside an annotated source-line range in a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new annotation.
codly.annotation(body, ..fields)

// Equivalent set-rule for an annotation.
codly.annotation-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for an annotation.
codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args)


Codly creates this element while rendering [codly.new](new.md) and supplies its fields. body is the required positional content field; the remaining fields are named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Content attached to the annotation; none leaves only its number. |
| label | content \| none | Required; declared default: "todo" | Hidden reference-anchor content associated with a labelled annotation. Codly supplies this field. |
| height | length \| none | 0pt | Height of the brace spanning the rendered rows. |
| num | int \| none | 0 | Automatically assigned annotation number. |
| numbering | function \| none | numbering.with("(1)") | Formats num; use none to hide the number. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] References need a labelled figure.
> An annotation label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically.

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Annotation ranges count one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive.

Codly emits one annotation element for a configured line range. Range endpoints are one-indexed source-line positions, independent of displayed line-number offsets; annotation ranges cannot overlap. Use [codly.annotation-config](../types/annotation-config.md) to configure a range.

[codly.annotation-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields on generated annotations in scope; [codly.annotation-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the generated element.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: show-annotation-number
  label: Show annotation number
  default: true

codly.new(
  py
  prepare()
  result = compute()
  print(result)
  cleanup()
  ,
  annotations: ((
    start: 2,
    end: 4,
    content: [Computes and displays the result],
    numbering: if show-annotation-number { n => [(n)] } else { none },
  ),),
