title: bubble
text:
codly.bubble

A pointed callout bubble rendered next to a source line, with independent defaults for its paint, dimensions, spacing, and pointer.

 Signature

typst code
// A codly pointed callout bubble.
codly.bubble(
  body,
  gap: 0.5em,
  pointer-align: "center",
  pointer-size: 0.4em,
  pointer-height: auto,
  pointer-width: auto,
  pointer-offset: 0pt,
  align: center,
  fill: luma(245),
  stroke: 0.6pt + luma(80),
  inset: (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em),
  outset: 0pt,
  radius: 2pt,
  width: auto,
  line: int,
  pointer: int,
  placement: "below"
)


[codly.bubble](signature) is the generated element type for pointed callouts. Its body is positional; line and pointer are required named fields when representing the element directly. In normal use, create bubbles by setting pointer on a callouts entry.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | required, positional | Content displayed inside the bubble. |
| gap | length \| dictionary | 0.5em | Minimum separation from neighboring bubbles; a length applies on both axes, or use (x: ..., y: ...). |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" | "center" | Preferred alignment of the bubble around its source character; placement clamps it to the row. |
| pointer-size | length | 0.4em | Default pointer height and half its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Pointer height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full pointer base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |
| pointer-offset | length | 0pt | Horizontal shift of the pointer tip from its source character; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| align | alignment | center | Alignment of the bubble content. |
| fill | paint \| none | luma(245) | Fill shared by the bubble and pointer. |
| stroke | stroke \| none | 0.6pt + luma(80) | The bubble's single outline, including its pointer. |
| inset | length \| dictionary | (x: 0.5em, y: 0.3em) | Padding inside the bubble. |
| outset | length \| dictionary | 0pt | Extra paint extent around the body; reserved in the row. |
| radius | length | 2pt | Bubble corner radius. |
| width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content, bounded by the available row. |
| line | int | required, named | One-indexed source line attached to the bubble. |
| pointer | int | required, named | Source character anchor, one-indexed, with 0 at the start of the line. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" | "below" | Side of the source line on which to place the bubble. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Bubbles can share a row
> Consecutive bubbles on the same side of a source line share a row when their outlines fit. If they collide, Codly places them in separate lanes in declaration order; adjust gap or width to control the spacing and wrapping.

The bubble and arrow use one outline and fill. Content wraps at the available width. Negative dimensions, pointer sizes, insets, and outsets are rejected. Styling defaults set on [codly.bubble](signature) are inherited by generated bubbles; explicit [codly.callout](callout.md) settings and then entry-level bubble settings take precedence. A callout with pointer: none does not produce a bubble.

 Rules

[codly.bubble-set_(..args)](signature) sets styling defaults for generated bubbles. [codly.bubble-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs a show rule for generated bubbles; its first argument is replacement content or a callback.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: pointer
  label: Pointer position
  default: 17
  min: 0
  max: 26
  step: 1

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.bubble-set_(fill: aqua.lighten(75%), radius: 6pt, width: 125pt)
codly.new(
  js
  let total = subtotal + tax
  ,
  callouts: ((
    line: 1,
    pointer: pointer,
    body: [The final amount includes tax.],
  ),),
)


 Example: Custom Show Rule
typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.bubble-show_(it => {
  box(stroke: red, it)
})

codly.new(
  js
  let total = subtotal + tax
  ,
  callouts: ((
    line: 1,
    pointer: 17,
    body: [The final amount includes tax.],
  ),),
)

title: callout
text:
codly.callout

A row attached to a source line in a Codly code block; it can be plain text or a pointed bubble.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new callout.
codly.callout(
  body,
  line: int,
  align: auto,
  breakable: auto,
  inset: auto,
  fill: auto,
  stroke: auto,
  source-indent: false,
  placement: "below",

  // Parameters for the bubble if any.
  bubble-gap: auto,
  bubble-align: auto,
  bubble-fill: auto,
  bubble-stroke: auto,
  bubble-inset: auto,
  bubble-outset: auto,
  bubble-radius: auto,
  bubble-width: auto,
  
  // Parameters for the bubble's pointer if used.
  pointer: none,
  pointer-align: auto,
  pointer-size: auto,
  pointer-height: auto,
  pointer-width: auto,
  pointer-offset: auto,
)


body is positional. line is required and named. Normally, callouts are created by entries in the callouts field; see [codly.callout-config](../types/callout-config.md).

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | required, positional | Content displayed in the row or bubble. |
| line | int | required, named | One-indexed source line to attach to. |
| align | alignment \| auto \| none | auto | Alignment of the callout cell; auto inherits the code block's cell alignment. |
| breakable | bool \| auto \| none | auto | Whether the callout cell may break across pages; pointed bubble groups stay together. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Inset of the callout cell. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | auto | Fill of the callout cell. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Stroke of the callout cell. |
| source-indent | bool | false | Aligns a plain callout with source indentation while reserving gutter columns; pointed bubbles remain character-anchored. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" | "below" | Side of the attached source line. |
| bubble-gap | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Minimum separation between bubbles; use a length for both axes or (x: ..., y: ...). |
| pointer-offset | length \| auto | auto | Horizontal shift of the tip from the source character; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| bubble-align | alignment \| auto | auto | Bubble content alignment, independent of the cell alignment. |
| bubble-fill | paint \| none \| auto | auto | Fill shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-stroke | stroke \| none \| auto | auto | Single outline shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-inset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Padding inside the bubble. |
| bubble-outset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Extra paint extent around the bubble body, reserved in the row. |
| bubble-radius | length \| auto | auto | Bubble corner radius. |
| bubble-width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content within the available row. |
| pointer | int \| none | none | Character anchor in the source line: one-based, with 0 at line start. Set to none for a plain row. |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| auto | auto | Preferred bubble alignment around the anchor; placement clamps it to the available row. |
| pointer-size | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height and half of its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Plain callouts can follow source indentation
> Set source-indent: true to align a plain callout with the source indentation while preserving the gutter columns. Pointed callouts stay anchored to their source character.

Callout lines are source-line coordinates, unaffected by displayed line-number offsets. Pointer positions count characters in the source line, with zero denoting its start; the pointer follows the rendered character when code wraps. Negative pointers, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are rejected. A bubble's body and arrow share one fill and outline, and bubble text wraps to its available width.

Unspecified or auto bubble styling inherits from [codly.bubble](bubble.md), after explicit [codly.callout](signature) styling. Entry values in callouts take precedence over the element's set-rule values. Explicit none disables bubble fill or stroke; pointer: none keeps a callout plain.

[codly.callout-set_(..args)](signature) sets defaults for callout cells and bubbles; [codly.callout-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs a show rule taking replacement content or a callback such as it => [it]. Bubble-specific defaults and show rules are documented on [codly.bubble](bubble.md).

 Example

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: source-indent
  label: Align plain callout to source indentation
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.callout-set_(source-indent: source-indent)
codly.new(
  py
  if ready:
    start()
  ,
  callouts: (
    (line: 1, body: [Plain callout aligned with the source.]),
    (line: 2, pointer: 3, body: [Pointing at start.]),
  ),
)

title: ref
text:
codly.ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> Line, highlight, and annotation references require the code block to sit inside a labelled figure; Codly discovers the figure label automatically.

Sets shared formatting for references to code lines, highlights, and annotations.

 Signature

typst code
codly.ref(body, by: "line", sep: "-", numbering: numbering.with("1"))
codly.ref-set_(..fields)


[codly.ref](signature) is an element definition; [codly.ref-set_(...)](signature) is a set-rule wrapper for its fields, not a separate element. There is no ref-show_: references render through native syntax and the show rules of the generated reference elements.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Content of the reference element. |
| by | "line" \| "item" \| none | "line" | Choose a displayed line number or an item label/content for highlight and annotation references. |
| sep | str \| content \| none | "-" | Content between the native reference to the code block and the line number or item. |
| numbering | function \| none | numbering.with("1") | Formats line numbers when by is "line"; none leaves the native block reference without a line suffix. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Choose what the reference shows.
> The shared by: "line" setting shows the displayed line number. by: "item" shows the highlight tag or annotation content instead.

> [!WARNING] Item references to highlights need a tag.
> When by: "item", each referenced highlight must define a tag; Codly reports an error if the tag is missing. Annotation item references use the annotation's content.

The fields in [codly.ref](signature) are shared defaults for [codly.line-ref](line-ref.md), [codly.highlight-ref](highlight-ref.md), and [codly.annotation-ref](annotation-ref.md). A field set directly on one of those generated reference elements takes precedence over the shared setting. by: "item" uses the highlight's tag or the annotation's content; line references always refer to a displayed line. Numbering callbacks receive the displayed line number. These references resolve to the containing code figure or block, so ordinary Typst reference formatting still applies to that target.

See [codly.line-ref](line-ref.md), [codly.highlight-ref](highlight-ref.md), and [codly.annotation-ref](annotation-ref.md) for the generated reference fields.

 Example

This figure labels a code block and an annotation. The reference to the annotation uses its content as the item suffix:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ")

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note and the line is @example:2.

title: line-ref
text:
codly.line-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> Put the code block inside a labelled figure to enable line references.
> Codly detects that figure label automatically, so omit the block-label
> argument from codly.new.

Formats native Typst references to displayed lines in labeled Codly code blocks.

 Signature

typst code
codly.line-ref(body, block: label, number: int, suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto)
codly.line-ref-set_(..args)
codly.line-ref-show_(it, ..args)


[codly.line-ref](signature) is a generated element definition; Codly creates it for line targets, so user code normally refers to those targets with @block:line rather than constructing the element. line-ref-set_(...) applies field defaults to generated line references in the current scope. line-ref-show_(it) installs a show rule; its first argument is the replacement callback or content, not field overrides.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | required | Internal reference body supplied by Typst. |
| block | label | required, named | Label of the containing code block. |
| number | int | required, named | Displayed line number. |
| suffix | content \| none | none | Optional suffix attached to the displayed line number. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Content between the native block reference and line number; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Formats the displayed line number; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings, while none leaves only the native block reference. |

 Behavior

The constructor is exported, but references are normally generated from native @block:line syntax; the element has no custom casts and cannot itself carry a label. The reference shows the block figure followed by the formatted line number — the displayed number, not a source position.

separator: auto and numbering: auto inherit [codly.ref](ref.md)'s sep and numbering settings. Explicit fields set through line-ref-set_ override those shared defaults for line references in scope. A numbering function receives the displayed line number. line-ref-show_ lets a show rule replace or wrap the generated reference; its callback receives the element.

See [codly.ref](ref.md) for shared reference defaults.

 Example

Labels a code block and refers to its second displayed line; the local set rule changes the separator and number format:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.line-ref-set_(separator: " line ", numbering: n => [Ln])

figure(caption: [A small code block])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
  )
] 

The reference points to line two of the block: @example:2.

title: highlight-ref
text:
codly.highlight-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> A highlight label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure.

[codly.highlight-ref](signature) declares the native reference element emitted for a labelled highlight.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a highlight reference element
codly.highlight-ref(
  body,
  block: label,
  line: int,
  by: "line" | "item",
  item: content | none = none,
  separator: auto | str | content = auto,
  numbering: auto | function | none = auto
)

// Set default fields for matching highlight references
codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args)

// Install a replacement callback or content for matching highlight references
codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args)


 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content \| none | Required, positional | Reference body supplied by Typst. |
| block | label | Required, named | Label of the containing code block. |
| line | int | Required, named | Displayed line number containing the highlight. |
| item | content \| none | none | Highlight tag used when by is "item". |
| by | "line" \| "item" | Required, named | Whether to show the line number or highlight tag. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Text between the block reference and this reference; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Formatter for line references; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |

 Behavior

Typst emits this element when a native reference targets a label on a highlight. It retains the reference to the containing figure or code block, so native figure numbering and links work. With by: "line", the formatter receives the displayed line number. With by: "item", the tag is shown and item must be present. A none formatter suppresses the numeric part of line references; item references still show their tag. The default separator and formatter come from [codly.ref](ref.md).

[codly.highlight-ref-set_(..args)](signature) sets fields for matching references; [codly.highlight-ref-show_(it, ..args)](signature) installs replacement content or a callback receiving the reference element.

 Example

typ preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.highlight-ref-set_(numbering: numbering.with("H1"))

The marked line is @marked.

figure(caption: [A labelled highlight])[
  codly.new(
    
    answer = 42
    ,
    highlights: ((line: 1, start: 0, end: 6, label:  ),),
  )
]

title: annotation-ref
text:
codly.annotation-ref

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure.
> An annotation label resolves only when the code block sits inside a labelled figure.

A native reference element created for a labelled annotation in a code block inside a figure.

 Signature

typst code
// Create a new annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref(body, block: label, line: int, item: content, by: "line" | "item", suffix: none, separator: auto, numbering: auto)

// Equivalent set-rule for an annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref-set_(..args)

// Override the show-rule for an annotation reference.
codly.annotation-ref-show_(it, ..args)


Codly creates this element when Typst resolves a native reference such as @note. Use annotation-ref-set_(...) to set fields in scope, or annotation-ref-show_(callback) to replace or transform its display.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content or none | required | Internal body of the native reference. |
| block | label | required | Label of the containing code block. |
| line | int | required | Displayed source line associated with the annotation. |
| item | content | required | Annotation content used for item references. |
| suffix | content or none | none | Optional suffix after the formatted line number. |
| by | "line" \| "item" | required | Whether the suffix shows a formatted line number or the annotation item. |
| separator | auto \| str \| content \| none | auto | Content between the native block reference and its suffix; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings. |
| numbering | auto \| function \| none | auto | Line-number formatter; auto uses [codly.ref](ref.md) settings and none omits the suffix in line mode. |

by, separator, and numbering can also be set for all generated references with [codly.ref](ref.md). Explicit fields on this element take precedence. In item mode, the annotation's content is used; numbering and suffix apply only to line mode. With line mode and numbering: none, the rendered reference contains just the native reference to the code block.

annotation-ref-show_ receives the generated reference element, so a callback can inspect or wrap it. For example, show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: it]) prefixes each displayed annotation reference while keeping its existing rendering.

 Example: Basic usage

With the default line mode, the reference appends the displayed line number to the figure reference:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note.



 Example: Item-based reference

With by: "item", the suffix is the annotation's content; the show rule adds a prefix:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.ref-set_(by: "item", sep: " — ")
show: codly.annotation-ref-show_(it => [Note: it])

figure(caption: [A code example])[
  codly.new(
    
    first line
    second line
    ,
    annotations: ((start: 2, label:  , content: [the note]),),
  )
] 

The annotation reference is @note.

title: sublang-block
text:
codly.sublang-block

> [!WARNING] Sublang blocks cost performance.
> Each sublang block requires re-parsing and introspection; heavy use slows compilation.

The generated element that holds one syntax-highlighted language range inside a Codly code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.sublang-block(body, idx)


Codly creates this element while rendering [codly.new](new.md). In normal use, configure language ranges with the block's sublangs field and [codly.sublang](../types/sublang.md), rather than constructing this element directly. Both required fields are positional in the generated element constructor.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| body | content | Required, positional | Raw block content highlighted with the range's language. |
| idx | int | Required, positional | Zero-based index of this range in the block's sublangs array. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Range indexes follow declaration order.
> idx is zero-based within one code block's sublangs array; it does not
> identify a source line or language key.

For each configured sublanguage range, Codly creates a raw block with that range's language and stores it in body. Its display keeps the syntax highlighting while attaching per-line metadata so the block renderer can reuse it.

 Example

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  sh
  > cat test.rs
  fn main() {
      println!("hello");
  }
  > exit

  ,
  sublangs: ((start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"),),
)

title: language
text:
codly.language

Defines the displayed name, color, and optional icon for a language badge in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.language(
  name: str | content,
  color: paint | none = none,
  icon: str | content | none = none,
)


name is required and named. Fields expecting this type also accept a string as shorthand for name, or a dictionary. Unknown fields are retained.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| name | str \| content | Required | Displayed language name. |
| color | paint \| none | none | Language color; none uses the badge's default color. |
| icon | str \| content \| none | none | Optional icon shown beside the name. |

The declaration preserves additional, unknown fields. They can provide language-specific overrides to [codly.lang](../components/lang.md) fields, such as radius or fill.

 Behavior

Use language definitions as values in the languages dictionary passed to [codly.lang-set_](../components/lang.mdsignature). The dictionary key must match the raw block's language tag. The settings apply within the show rule's scope. A definition's name, icon, and color customize the badge; an omitted definition falls back to the raw language tag. A definition's matching [codly.lang](../components/lang.md) style fields override the corresponding settings supplied to [codly.lang-set_](../components/lang.mdsignature).

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.lang-set_(languages: (
  rs: (name: [Rust], color: rgb("b7502a"), icon: "R"),
))
show raw.where(block: true): codly.new

rs
fn main() {
    println!("Hello, Rust!");
}

title: range
text:
codly.range

Selects an inclusive range of one-indexed source lines for a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.range(start, end: none)


start is positional and required. end is optional and may be passed positionally or by name.

 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | Required | First source line to display, counting from 1. |
| end | int \| none | none | Last source line to display, inclusive. none selects through the end of the block. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Range endpoints count source lines from one and include both start and
> end; displayed numbering offsets do not change them.

> [!TIP] Adjacent ranges merge.
> When several ranges are selected, Codly sorts them and merges overlapping
> or directly adjacent ranges before rendering.

Pass a range to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s range field, or pass several ranges to its ranges field. An open range such as [codly.range(3)](signature) continues through the final source line.

The constructor accepts positional arguments ([codly.range(2, 4)](signature)) or named arguments ([codly.range(start: 2, end: 4)](signature)). Implicit casts accept a one- or two-element array or a dictionary with start and optional end keys; unknown dictionary keys are rejected. Bounds are type-checked as integers (or none for end), with no positivity or ordering constraint.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  prepare()
  validate()
  transform()
  save()
  ,
  range: codly.range(2, 3),
)

title: skip
text:
codly.skip

Describes an explicit collapsed gap in a code block; pass it in [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s skips field.

 Signature

typst code
codly.skip(position, length: 1)


position is the required positional argument; length is optional and can be supplied positionally or by name.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| position | int | Required | One-indexed source line before which the skip row is inserted. |
| length | int | 1 | Number of omitted lines represented by the skip; added to subsequent displayed line numbers. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> position is a one-indexed source line, even when ranges or offsets
> change which lines appear. Position 2 inserts the gap before source line 2.

> [!TIP] Duplicate positions make one skip row.
> If multiple skips have the same position, Codly uses the first entry's
> length to adjust subsequent displayed line numbers.

The constructor accepts [codly.skip(position, length)](signature) or named fields. A dictionary casts using position and optional length; an array of one or two values casts positionally. The skips field sorts entries by position.

Explicit skips represent lines already omitted from the supplied source. They add a gap row and increase subsequent displayed numbers; they do not remove source lines. Use range or ranges with smart-skip to omit lines that are still present.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  first
  second
  third
  fourth
  ,
  skips: (codly.skip(2, 4),),
)

title: highlighted-line
text:
codly.highlighted-line

Describes one whole line to highlight in [codly.new](../components/new.md).

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlighted-line(line, color: none)


line is required and positional; color is optional and positional or named.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed displayed line number to highlight. |
| color | none \| paint | none | Optional paint for this line; none uses the next color from [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md). |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Uses displayed line numbers
> line refers to the number shown in the document, including offsets and numbering changes from skips. A source line with no displayed number cannot be selected this way.

> [!TIP] Explicit colors leave the palette cycle untouched
> A supplied color is used directly. Entries with color: none take and advance the next [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md) palette color.

The constructor also accepts named fields. The value casts from an integer, a dictionary with line and optional color, or an array of one or two values in field order; other values and array lengths fail to cast.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  prepare()
  run()
  cleanup()
  ,
  highlighted: (codly.highlighted-line(2, yellow.lighten(75%)),),
)

title: unnumbered-line
text:
codly.unnumbered-line

Selects a source line to show without its line number, optionally putting content in the number cell.

 Signature

typst code
codly.unnumbered-line(line, fill: [])


Both arguments are positional: line is required and fill is optional.

 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed source line to display without a line number. |
| fill | content | [] | Content to display in the number cell instead. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed source line, even when a range or offset changes its
> displayed position or number.

Pass entries to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s unnumbered field. The constructor takes positional arguments; implicit casts accept an integer, a one- or two-element array, or a dictionary with line and optional fill fields.

An unnumbered line does not advance the displayed number sequence, so later numbered lines remain contiguous. Consecutive unnumbered lines can be referenced with labels such as @block:l2p1 and @block:l2p2, where the l number is the preceding displayed number and p counts the unnumbered lines after it.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

figure(caption: [Unnumbered source lines])[
  codly.new(
    
    first
    label:
    second
    end
    last
    ,
    unnumbered: (
      codly.unnumbered-line(2, [↳]),
      codly.unnumbered-line(4),
    ),
  )
] 

The unnumbered lines are @block:l1p1 and @block:l2p1.

title: smart-skip
text:
codly.smart-skip

Configures which omitted source-line gaps appear as collapsed skip rows when a code block displays selected ranges.

 Signature

typst code
codly.smart-skip(
  first: bool | none = none,
  last: bool | none = none,
  rest: bool | none = none,
)


All fields are named and optional.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| first | bool \| none | none | Include a skip when source lines before the first selected range are omitted. |
| last | bool \| none | none | Include a skip when source lines after the last selected range are omitted. |
| rest | bool \| none | none | Include skips for omitted lines between selected ranges or otherwise in the middle of the block. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Automatic skips mark gaps between displayed source ranges; they do not
> change the source-line coordinates used by those ranges.

Pass this value to [codly.new](../components/new.md)'s smart-skip field. A boolean casts to the same value for all three fields. A dictionary casts to this type: omitted rest defaults to false, and omitted first or last inherits rest. Thus (rest: true, first: false) enables middle skips and trailing skips, while suppressing a leading skip. With all three fields false, no automatic skips are inserted. A skip row is inserted only for a discontinuity in the displayed source lines; its represented length is the number of omitted lines.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: show-middle-gap
  label: Show the omitted middle lines
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  python
  def prepare():
      load_data()
      validate()
      transform()
      save()
      report()
      cleanup()
  ,
  ranges: ((2, 3), (6, 7)),
  smart-skip: codly.smart-skip(first: false, last: false, rest: show-middle-gap),
)

title: highlight-config
text:
codly.highlight-config

Describes one character-level highlight on a source line in a Codly code block. See [codly.new](../components/new.md) for the block's highlights field.

 Signature

typst code
codly.highlight-config(line, start: none, end: none, fill: none, tag: none, inset: none, baseline: none, clip: none, outset: none, radius: none, label: none, stroke: none, depth: none)


line is the required positional field; every other field is named. A dictionary with a line key can also be cast to this type.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed displayed line number to highlight; must be greater than zero. |
| start | none \| int | none | Zero-indexed character position where the highlight starts; none becomes 0. |
| end | none \| int | none | Exclusive zero-indexed end bound; none extends to the end of the line. |
| fill | none \| paint \| function | none | Explicit paint, or a callback receiving the next palette paint; none uses the configured palette. |
| tag | none \| str \| content | none | Optional tag displayed with the highlight. |
| inset | none \| length \| dictionary | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s inset. |
| baseline | none \| length \| auto | none | Overrides the highlight box baseline; auto preserves the content baseline. |
| clip | none \| bool | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s clip. |
| outset | none \| length \| dictionary | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s outset. |
| radius | none \| length | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s radius. |
| label | none \| label | none | Label for referencing this highlight; labels apply only when the code block is inside a figure. |
| stroke | none \| stroke \| function | none | Overrides [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md)'s stroke. |
| depth | none \| int | none | Controls stacking when highlights overlap; larger values appear on top. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed displayed line number, including any offset.
> start and end are zero-indexed character positions, and end is exclusive.

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure
> To reference a highlight, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure.

The constructor and dictionary cast normalize omitted or none bounds to start: 0 and an end bound covering the rest of the line. Explicit bounds must be nonnegative; line must be positive. Character positions are zero-indexed and the end is exclusive, unlike the inclusive, one-indexed source-line ranges. A fill paint is used directly and does not consume a palette entry; a callback receives the next palette paint. Highlights using none also consume the next palette entry. An empty configured palette is invalid. Local style fields override the corresponding [codly.highlight](../components/highlight.md) settings when provided.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  let answer = 42
  ,
  highlights: (codly.highlight-config(1, start: 4, end: 10, fill: yellow.lighten(65%), tag: "value"),),
)

title: annotation-config
text:
codly.annotation-config

Describes an annotation attached to one or more one-indexed source lines in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.annotation-config(start, end: none, content: none, label: none, numbering: n => [n])


 Parameters

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | required | First source line covered by the annotation; must be greater than zero. |
| end | int \| none | none | Last covered line. none is normalized to start; otherwise it must be positive and at least start. |
| content | content \| none | none | Showable content displayed beside the annotation; none leaves only its number. |
| label | label \| none | none | Label for referencing this annotation when its code block is inside a figure. |
| numbering | function \| none | n => [n] | Function formatting the annotation number. Set to none to hide the number. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> start and end are one-indexed source lines, and end is inclusive. Displayed line-number offsets do not change the covered source lines.

> [!WARNING] References need a labelled figure
> To reference an annotation, give it a label and place its code block inside a labelled figure. Codly discovers the figure label automatically.

> [!WARNING] Annotation ranges cannot overlap.
> Two annotations cannot cover the same source line. Because end is
> inclusive, the next annotation must start after the previous one's end.

The positional start argument is required. The constructor also accepts a dictionary with a start key. Dictionary and constructor inputs are type-checked, then normalized: a missing or none end becomes start, and missing content becomes none. start and a supplied end must be positive, and end must not precede start.

Annotations are passed in the code block's annotations array.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  prepare()
  result = compute()
  print(result)
  cleanup()
  ,
  annotations: (
    codly.annotation-config(
      2,
      end: 3,
      content: [These lines compute and display the result.],
    ),
  ),
)

title: callout-config
text:
codly.callout-config

Describes a content row attached to a source line in a code block. Use it in the callouts field of [codly.new](../components/new.md).

 Signature

typst code
codly.callout-config(line: int, body: content, align: auto, breakable: auto, inset: auto, fill: auto, stroke: auto, source-indent: auto, placement: auto, bubble-gap: auto, pointer: auto, pointer-align: auto, pointer-size: auto, pointer-height: auto, pointer-width: auto, pointer-offset: auto, bubble-align: auto, bubble-fill: auto, bubble-stroke: auto, bubble-inset: auto, bubble-outset: auto, bubble-radius: auto, bubble-width: auto)


All fields are named. A dictionary with line and body keys can also be used as a callout entry.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default / required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| line | int | Required | One-indexed source line to attach the callout to; must be greater than zero. |
| body | content | Required | Content displayed in the callout row. |
| align | alignment \| auto \| none | auto | Alignment of the callout cell; auto inherits the element setting. |
| breakable | bool \| auto \| none | auto | Whether the cell may break across pages; auto inherits the element setting. |
| inset | length \| dictionary \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell inset; auto inherits the element setting. |
| fill | paint \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell fill; auto inherits the element setting. |
| stroke | stroke \| auto \| none | auto | Callout cell stroke; auto inherits the element setting. |
| source-indent | bool \| auto | auto | Aligns a plain callout with its source indentation while reserving gutter columns. Pointed bubbles remain anchored to their character. |
| placement | "above" \| "below" \| auto | auto | Side of the source line for the row or bubble. |
| bubble-gap | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Minimum distance between neighboring bubbles; use a length for both axes or (x: length, y: length). |
| pointer | int \| none \| auto | auto | Character anchor in the source line: one-indexed, with 0 at line start. none disables the bubble. |
| pointer-align | "start" \| "center" \| "end" \| auto | auto | Preferred bubble alignment around its source character; placement clamps it to the row. |
| pointer-size | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height and half of its base width. |
| pointer-height | length \| auto | auto | Arrow height; auto uses pointer-size. |
| pointer-width | length \| auto | auto | Full arrow base width; auto uses twice pointer-size. |
| pointer-offset | length \| auto | auto | Horizontal shift of the arrow tip from the character anchor; positive is right, negative is left, and the tip is clamped to the bubble. |
| bubble-align | alignment \| auto | auto | Alignment of bubble content, independent of callout cell alignment. |
| bubble-fill | paint \| none \| auto | auto | Fill shared by the bubble and arrow. |
| bubble-stroke | stroke \| none \| auto | auto | The bubble's single outline. |
| bubble-inset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Padding inside the bubble. |
| bubble-outset | length \| dictionary \| auto | auto | Extra paint extent around the padded body, reserved in the row. |
| bubble-radius | length \| auto | auto | Bubble corner radius. |
| bubble-width | length \| ratio \| auto | auto | Preferred padded body width; auto fits content, bounded by the available row. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> line is a one-indexed source line. pointer is a one-indexed character position after any diff marker is removed; 0 points to the start of the line.

> [!WARNING] Pointed bubble groups stay together
> Bubbles attached to a source line stay together on one page, so a group may move as a unit at a page break.

An entry's auto style values inherit from [codly.callout](../components/callout.md); bubble styles can then inherit from [codly.bubble](../components/bubble.md). Explicit entry values take precedence. Cell fill and stroke accept none to disable painting. A pointed bubble uses one shared outline and paint for its body and arrow, and wraps its content at the available width.

Pointer positions count characters in the source line after a diff marker is removed; unlike highlight bounds, they are one-indexed, with zero denoting the start. The pointer follows the rendered character when source text wraps. Consecutive bubbles on the same side with matching cell styles share a row when their outlines fit; overlaps use another lane in declaration order.

Negative pointer positions, dimensions, insets, outsets, and gaps are invalid. bubble-gap dictionaries accept only x and y, whose omitted values default to 0.5em.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: slider
  name: bubble-width
  label: Bubble width
  default: 120pt
  unit: pt
  min: 80
  max: 180
  step: 10


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  if ready:
    start()
  ,
  callouts: (
    codly.callout-config(
      line: 2,
      pointer: 5,
      body: [This call runs when the input is ready.],
      bubble-width: bubble-width,
      bubble-fill: aqua.lighten(80%),
    ),
  ),
)

title: gutter-column
text:
codly.gutter-column

Defines one independently styled column beside a code block. Use it in gutters to show source-line labels, markers, or other row-specific content.

 Signature

typst code
codly.gutter-column(
  values: array  | function,
  width: auto | length | ratio | fraction = auto,
  align: auto | alignment = auto,
  inset: auto | length | dictionary = auto,
  stroke: auto | stroke | dictionary | none = auto,
  fill: auto | paint | array  | function | none = auto,
  text: dictionary = (:),
)


values is required and named. Arrays and functions can also be passed directly as gutter column specifications; dictionaries are cast to this type.

 Parameters

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| values | array  or function | Required | Values to display, or a callback that returns a value for a rendered row. |
| width | auto, length, ratio, or fraction | auto | Column width. |
| align | auto or alignment | auto | Cell alignment. |
| inset | auto, length, or dictionary | auto | Cell inset. |
| stroke | auto, stroke, dictionary, or none | auto | Cell stroke. |
| fill | auto, paint, array , function, or none | auto | Cell fill, a row-indexed fill palette, or a row callback. |
| text | dictionary | (:) | Arguments passed to text when displaying a value. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Array values follow source lines
> An array entry at index 0 supplies source line 1, even with ranges or
> offsets. Missing entries and none leave the gutter cell empty.

> [!TIP] Use a callback for rendered-row logic
> Only code and skip rows have gutter cells. A callback receives both
> source-line and kind, so it can handle skip rows separately from code.

A callback receives the rendered row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, number, and text. index counts displayed rows, including headers and callouts; source-line is one-based for source rows and none for generated rows. Callbacks may return content, strings, numbers, or none.

Values are validated when resolved, and width must be non-negative. auto alignment and insets inherit the number column's settings; fill: auto follows the body row. A fill callback also receives the row dictionary, with text populated from the source line where available.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  let answer = 42
  print(answer)
  ,
  gutters: (
    codly.gutter-column(
      values: row => if row.kind == "code" {
        str(row.source-line) + ". " + row.text
      } else { none },
      align: right,
      inset: (left: 4pt, right: 8pt),
      fill: gray.lighten(90%),
    ),
  ),
)

title: diff
text:
codly.diff

Configures automatic parsing, syntax highlighting, gutters, and row fills for raw blocks whose language is diff-  or diff, .

 Signature

typst code
codly.diff(
  enabled: bool = true,
  added-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("dafbe1"),
  removed-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ffebe9"),
  meta-fill: auto | paint | function = rgb("ddf4ff"),
  context-fill: auto | paint | function = auto,
  numbers: bool = true,
  markers: bool = true,
  added-marker: str | content = "+",
  removed-marker: str | content = "−",
  old-offset: int = 0,
  new-offset: int = 0,
)


The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Enables diff processing. |
| added-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("dafbe1") | Fill for added rows. |
| removed-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("ffebe9") | Fill for removed rows. |
| meta-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | rgb("ddf4ff") | Fill for patch metadata rows. |
| context-fill | auto \| paint \| function \| none | auto | Fill for unchanged rows; auto follows the ordinary row fill. |
| numbers | bool | true | Shows automatic old-side and new-side line-number gutters. |
| markers | bool | true | Shows the automatic added/removed marker gutter. |
| added-marker | str \| content | "+" | Marker shown for added rows. |
| removed-marker | str \| content | "−" | Marker shown for removed rows. |
| old-offset | int | 0 | Added to old-side source line numbers. |
| new-offset | int | 0 | Added to new-side source line numbers. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Use the patch language prefix
> Set the raw block language to diff-  or diff, , such as diff-py or diff,py, to enable patch parsing and highlight the changed code as Python.

> [!NOTE] Patch line coordinates
> References and line-based settings use displayed patch-row numbers. Highlight and callout character positions count code after the diff marker is removed.

> [!WARNING] Combined merge diffs are unsupported
> Codly parses unified patches, including multiple files and hunks, but not combined merge diff format.

With the block-level diff setting at auto (the default), Codly detects both prefixes and strips them for syntax highlighting. Old and new source views are rendered separately, so removed code does not affect new-side syntax state. Unified patches may contain multiple files and hunks, each highlighted independently. A non-patch snippet may use  , +, and - prefixes for context, added, and removed rows.

For fenced blocks, diff-py works in Typst 0.15; use raw(..., lang: "diff,py") on versions without comma support in language tags.

Each fill accepts a paint, none, or auto; auto uses the ordinary row fill. A callback receives the row with a diff record containing kind, old, and new line coordinates, as well as the row's usual fields. Explicit highlights take precedence over diff fills. Setting diff: false or diff: none disables processing; setting it to true enables the default configuration. Custom gutters replace the automatic old/new/marker columns.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: diff-enabled
  label: Process the diff
  default: true


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  diff-py
   shared
  -old = 1
  +new = 2
   tail
  ,
  diff: if diff-enabled { auto } else { false },
)

title: sublang
text:
codly.sublang

Assigns a syntax-highlighting language to an inclusive range of source lines in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.sublang(
  start: int,
  end: int,
  lang: str,
)


All fields are required and named. The value can also be supplied as a dictionary.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| start | int | Required | First source line in the range, counting from 1. |
| end | int | Required | Last source line in the range, inclusive. |
| lang | str | Required | Syntax-highlighting language key used for these lines. |

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Source coordinates
> Sublanguage ranges count one-indexed source lines and include both
> endpoints, independent of displayed line-number offsets.

> [!TIP] Highlighting preserves the original lines.
> Codly applies each range's syntax language to its source lines while keeping
> their text and positions in the outer code block.

Pass one or more [codly.sublang](signature) values in the sublangs argument to [codly.new](../components/new.md). start must be positive and end at least start; invalid ranges raise an error. Lines outside the ranges keep the raw block's language. Ranges may also be supplied as dictionaries with the same three fields.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  sh
  echo before
  fn answer() {
      42
  }
  echo after

  ,
  sublangs: (
    (start: 2, end: 4, lang: "rs"),
  ),
)

title: rainbow
text:
codly.rainbow

Configures syntax-aware coloring for matching code delimiters by nesting depth.

 Signature

typst code
codly.rainbow(
  enabled: bool = true,
  palette: array  = (...),
  pairs: array  = ("()", "[]", "{}"),
  depth-offset: int = 0,
  unmatched: color | none = none,
  code-scopes: str = ...,
  ignore-scopes: str = ...,
)


The value can also be a dictionary with these fields, or a boolean that sets enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Enables delimiter coloring. |
| palette | array  | Built-in palette | Colors cycled by nesting depth; must not be empty. |
| pairs | array of "()" \| "[]" \| "{}" | ("()", "[]", "{}") | Delimiter pairs recognized for nesting. |
| depth-offset | int | 0 | Adds an offset to the nesting depth before choosing a palette color; must be nonnegative. |
| unmatched | color \| none | none | Color for unmatched delimiters; none leaves their syntax color unchanged. |
| code-scopes | str | Built-in selectors | Syntax scope selectors classified as code by the rainbow pass. |
| ignore-scopes | str | Built-in selectors | Syntax scope selectors excluded from delimiter coloring, such as strings and comments. |

 Behavior

> [!WARNING] The palette must be nonempty.
> An empty palette or a negative depth-offset causes a compilation error.

> [!TIP] Adjust scopes for unusual grammars.
> code-scopes and ignore-scopes replace the built-in selectors. Customize
> them when a language classifies delimiters differently from the defaults.

Set rainbow on [codly.new](../components/new.md) or in [codly.set_](../components/new.mdbehavior) to configure blocks in that scope. true enables the defaults and false disables the pass. Delimiters are colored according to nesting depth, cycling through palette; depth-offset shifts the starting color. Only pairs listed in pairs contribute to nesting. Unclosed openers and unmatched closers use unmatched when it is a color; otherwise they retain their syntax highlighting.

The pass uses syntax scopes to find code and ignore literals and comments; sublanguage regions are processed with their own nesting stack.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: rainbow-enabled
  label: Color delimiters
  default: true
- type: select
  name: rainbow-pairs
  label: Delimiter pairs
  default: '("()", "[]", "{}")'
  options:
    - label: All pairs
      value: '("()", "[]", "{}")'
    - label: Braces only
      value: '("{}",)'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  rs
  fn main() {
      let items = [1, 2, 3];
      println!("{}", items[0]);
  }
  ,
  rainbow: if rainbow-enabled {
    (palette: (rgb("d73a49"), rgb("005cc5"), rgb("22863a")), pairs: rainbow-pairs)
  } else {
    false
  },
)

title: indent-guides
text:
codly.indent-guides

Configures optional vertical guides at complete indentation levels in a code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.indent-guides(
  enabled: bool = true,
  width: auto | int = auto,
  blank-lines: bool = true,
  rainbow: auto | bool = auto,
  palette: auto | array  = auto,
  depth-offset: auto | int = auto,
  color: color = luma(70%),
  thickness: length = 0.5pt,
  x-offset: length = 0pt,
)


The fields can also be supplied as a dictionary. A boolean casts to enabled.

 Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| enabled | bool | true | Draws indentation guides when enabled. |
| width | auto \| int | auto | Spaces per indentation level. auto votes on observed indentation changes. |
| blank-lines | bool | true | Continues shared guide levels across interior blank lines. |
| rainbow | auto \| bool | auto | Colors guides by level; auto follows whether delimiter rainbow coloring is enabled. |
| palette | auto \| array  | auto | Nonempty colors for rainbow guides; auto shares the delimiter palette. |
| depth-offset | auto \| int | auto | Nonnegative palette offset; auto shares the delimiter offset. |
| color | color | luma(70%) | Guide color when rainbow coloring is disabled. |
| thickness | length | 0.5pt | Positive stroke thickness. |
| x-offset | length | 0pt | Horizontal guide shift; positive moves right and negative moves left. Supports em lengths. |

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Check the inferred indentation step
> width: auto chooses the most frequently observed change in leading spaces; ties favor the smaller step, and no observed step falls back to four spaces. Set width explicitly when the source uses a known indentation size.

> [!NOTE] Only complete levels get guides
> A guide is drawn for each complete width-sized level. Indentation that does not reach the next complete level has no guide.

Set the block-level indent-guides field to true for defaults, false to disable inherited guides for one block, or a configuration to customize them. Interior blank lines continue only the levels shared by the surrounding nonblank lines when blank-lines is true; leading and trailing blank lines have no inferred guides.

With rainbow: auto, guides use delimiter rainbow colors when delimiter rainbow is enabled. Explicit rainbow: true enables palette coloring; false uses color. An explicit palette or depth offset overrides values inherited from delimiter rainbow settings. The palette must not be empty, width must be positive or auto, depth offset must be nonnegative or auto, and thickness must be positive. Invalid field types are rejected by the declared types.

Guides follow source indentation and extend across wrapped visual rows when smart indentation is enabled. x-offset shifts all guides horizontally without changing source columns.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: switch
  name: guides-enabled
  label: Show indentation guides
  default: true
- type: select
  name: guide-width
  label: Spaces per level
  default: '4'
  options:
    - label: Two spaces
      value: '2'
    - label: Four spaces
      value: '4'
    - label: Eight spaces
      value: '8'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  text
  root
      child
          leaf
      sibling
  root
  ,
  indent-guides: if guides-enabled { (width: guide-width) } else { false },
)

title: Themes and helpers
text:
Themes and helpers

Use themes to apply consistent component styles and info to inspect a labelled block in context.

> [!TIP] Apply themes in scope.
> Use show: codly.theme(...) before the code blocks you want to style.
> Put the rule inside a content block to limit it to that part of the document.

- [codly.theme](theme.md)
- [codly.themes](themes.md)
- [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md)
- [codly.info](info.md)

title: theme
text:
codly.theme

Returns scoped set and show rules that apply a built-in or custom theme to Codly elements.

 Signature

typst code
codly.theme(..options)


 Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| preset (positional) | str or dictionary | "thesis" | Built-in theme name or a theme dictionary. At most one positional value is accepted. |
| Named options | See [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) | None | Shared tokens and element dictionaries forwarded to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md). |

The built-in presets are "thesis", "dark", "clean", "github-light", "solarized-light", and "one-light". The "thesis" preset follows Codly's ordinary visual defaults. See [codly.themes](themes.md) for the preset dictionaries and [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) for supported shared tokens, element dictionaries, and merge behavior.

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Theme only Codly content.
> The theme's typography and syntax colors apply inside Codly blocks; ordinary raw text outside them keeps its own styling.

Use the returned function as a show rule, commonly show: codly.theme("dark"). It applies scoped set rules to Codly's block, line, number, language, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, and annotation elements, along with their typography and syntax colors.

Named options are passed to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md), which validates names and values and combines them with the selected preset. Explicit element fields and later local set rules keep their normal precedence.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: theme-preset
  label: Theme
  default: '"github-light"'
  options:
    - label: Thesis
      value: '"thesis"'
    - label: Dark
      value: '"dark"'
    - label: Clean
      value: '"clean"'
    - label: GitHub Light
      value: '"github-light"'
    - label: Solarized Light
      value: '"solarized-light"'
    - label: One Light
      value: '"one-light"'


typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.theme(theme-preset)
codly.new(
  py
  def double(value):
      return value  2
  ,
  header: [example.py],
)

title: themes
text:
codly.themes

The built-in theme dictionaries, keyed by preset name; use [codly.theme](theme.md) to render one or [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) to derive a reusable configuration.

 Signature

typst code
codly.themes: dictionary


Its six keys are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. Each value is a theme dictionary. thesis is Codly's default appearance.

| Preset | Appearance |
| --- | --- |
| thesis | Codly's ordinary defaults, with language-colored badges and a light header. |
| dark | Dark editor palette with light text and syntax colors. |
| clean | Unboxed code with muted text and unpainted language badges. |
| github-light | GitHub light editor palette. |
| solarized-light | Solarized light editor palette. |
| one-light | One Light editor palette. |

 Theme dictionary keys

The theme loader accepts these shared token keys and element-section keys. Unknown top-level keys are rejected.

| Kind | Keys | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shared token | foreground, muted, fill, accent, stroke, radius, inset | Main text, subdued text, code-line fill, accent color, outline, corner radius, and inner spacing. |
| Shared token | header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill | Fills for headers, footers, and callout bubbles. |
| Shared token | syntax, highlight-fill, highlight-colors, language-colors | Raw-code syntax theme, highlight fill, highlight color or palette, and whether language badges use their language colors. |
| Element section | block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation | A dictionary of settings for that Codly element. Fields within a section follow that element's settings; its text field accepts native Typst text settings. |

The public theme dictionary can be inspected or selected by key. For the exact merge behavior and validation when creating a custom dictionary, see [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md).

 Behavior

> [!TIP] Derive a custom preset.
> Pass a value such as codly.themes.dark as base to [codly.define-theme](define-theme.md) to start a custom theme from that preset.

The preset entries are complete theme dictionaries; looking up a preset does not apply it to the document by itself.

 Example: Basic Usage

Renders one block per preset for side-by-side comparison:

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

let source = py
def double(value):
    return value  2

grid(
  columns: (1fr, 1fr),
  gutter: 6pt,
  ..codly.themes.keys().map(name => {
    show: codly.theme(name)
    codly.new(source, header: [name])
  }),
)

title: define-theme
text:
codly.define-theme

Build a reusable theme dictionary by inheriting a built-in preset or another theme, then applying named token and element-setting overrides.

 Signature

typst code
codly.define-theme(base: "thesis", ..overrides)


base is named and defaults to "thesis"; overrides are named arguments. Positional arguments are not accepted.

 Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | str or dictionary | "thesis" | A preset name or an existing theme dictionary. The built-in names are thesis, dark, clean, github-light, solarized-light, and one-light. |
| foreground | paint or auto | inherited | Text color for code; auto follows the surrounding text. |
| muted | paint or auto | inherited | Muted text color, including line numbers; auto follows the resolved foreground. |
| fill | auto, paint or none, array of paints or none, or function | inherited | Source-line fill. An array cycles by displayed row; a function receives a row dictionary with index, kind, source-line, and number. |
| accent | paint | inherited | Main accent, including the language badge's default color and (unless explicitly overridden) the first highlight color. |
| stroke | stroke | inherited | Default outline for code elements. |
| radius | length | inherited | Default corner radius. |
| inset | length or dictionary | inherited | Default code-line inset. |
| header-fill, footer-fill, bubble-fill | paint or none | inherited | Backgrounds for the header, footer, and callout bubbles. |
| syntax | auto, str, path, or bytes | inherited | TextMate plist theme for raw-code syntax highlighting. |
| highlight-fill | function | inherited | Callback receiving a highlight color and returning its fill. |
| highlight-colors | paint or nonempty array of paints | inherited | Default highlight color, or a palette cycled by highlights. |
| language-colors | bool | inherited | Whether language badges use their language-specific colors. |
| block, line, number, lang, file, header, footer, highlight, callout, bubble, annotation | dictionary | inherited | Overrides settable fields on the corresponding Codly element. The text entry in a section is a dictionary of native Typst text settings. |

All defaults are inherited from the selected base. Token names and section names are the complete supported top-level keys. Within a section, use fields supported by the corresponding Codly element. The fill callback's row dictionary uses a zero-based displayed-row index; kind is code, skip, or callout, while source-line and number are none for generated rows or numbers that are not displayed.

 Behavior

> [!NOTE] Accent also updates the first highlight color.
> If you override accent without supplying highlight-colors, the new accent replaces the first inherited highlight color. An explicit palette takes precedence.

> [!WARNING] Highlight palettes cannot be empty.
> Passing highlight-colors: () causes a compilation error.

The result is a complete dictionary, not a show rule. It starts with the thesis defaults, merges a preset or dictionary base, then merges the named overrides. Section dictionaries merge one level deep, so separate fields such as header: (fill: red) and header: (align: left) can be combined when deriving a theme. Values inside those fields, including callbacks and nested dictionaries, are replaced as complete values.

An unknown preset or top-level key raises an error. Every section override must be a dictionary.

Pass the returned dictionary to [codly.theme](../helpers/theme.md) to render with it. Theme rules are scoped: explicit element fields and later local set rules can override theme values. Section text settings are applied as text settings to text within that element.

 Example: Basic Usage

yaml widgets
- type: select
  name: accent
  label: Accent
  default: 'rgb("ef6c00")'
  options:
    - label: Orange
      value: 'rgb("ef6c00")'
    - label: Blue
      value: 'rgb("1565c0")'
    - label: Green
      value: 'rgb("2e7d32")'

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

let custom = codly.define-theme(
  base: "thesis",
  accent: accent,
  header: (fill: accent.lighten(80%), align: left),
)
show: codly.theme(custom)

codly.new(
  py
  return answer
  ,
  header: [Custom theme],
  highlights: ((line: 1),),
)

title: info
text:
codly.info

Read the source-line count and last displayed line number recorded for a labeled code block.

 Signature

typst code
codly.info(target) -> (last-number: int | none, lines: int)


 Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| target | label | required, positional | Label identifying the code block whose metadata to read. |

The returned dictionary has these fields:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| last-number | int or none | Last computed displayed line number, or none when the block has no numbered source line. |
| lines | int | Number of source lines in the block, including lines omitted from its displayed range. |

 Behavior

> [!WARNING] The target label must identify one code block.
> Labels resolving to zero or multiple locations, or to a location with no later Codly block record, cause a compilation error.

> [!NOTE] lines counts the full source.
> The count includes lines omitted by range; last-number reflects the selected range and offset.

Call [codly.info](signature) inside context, since it queries document content. The helper reads the first Codly block record after the label's location.

Unnumbered rows do not replace last-number. Passing the label as another block's offset adds this number to that block's numbering, so numbering can continue across blocks.

 Example: Basic Usage

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  
  first
  second
  ,
) 
codly.new(
  
  third
  ,
  offset:  ,
) 

context[
  First block: repr(codly.info( ))
]

title: ⚙️ Queries and show rules
text:
Queries and show rules

Use queries to inspect document elements, and show rules to customize how they render. This guide assumes you are comfortable with the [component fields](components/index.md).

 Choose the right tool

Codly's components are Elembic custom elements. Use the exported codly.e namespace to inspect fields, filter elements, or read scoped defaults. It provides the same Elembic version Codly uses, without a separate package import.

| Task | Tool |
| --- | --- |
| Set component defaults | show: codly.number-set_(...) and other -set_ helpers |
| Wrap or replace a component | show: codly.number-show_(it => ...) and other -show_ helpers |
| Read an element's resolved fields | codly.e.fields(it) |
| Find custom elements in the document | codly.e.query(codly.new) inside context |
| Read defaults in the current scope | codly.e.get(get => ...) |

The Codly helpers delegate to codly.e.set_ and codly.e.show_. For example, codly.number-show_(callback) is shorthand for codly.e.show_(codly.number, callback). Native set codly.number(...) does not configure an Elembic element.

 Query elements and inspect their fields

codly.e.query returns matching custom elements; codly.e.fields returns their field dictionaries. A .with(...) filter compares resolved field values. Use before: here() or after: here() to restrict the query by document location. [Elembic's query guide](https://pgbiel.github.io/elembic/elements/scripting/query.html) documents these filters and location bounds.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  print("hello")
  ,
  radius: 8pt,
)

context {
  let blocks = codly.e.query(codly.new.with(radius: 8pt), before: here())
  [Matching blocks: blocks.len().
  Language: codly.e.fields(blocks.first()).body.lang.]
}


Use native query( ) for labeled content and query(figure) for Typst figures. For custom elements, prefer codly.e.query: codly.selector() and codly.e.selector(codly.number) are native selectors intended for show rules. Their default selectors can match intermediate renderings; they are not reliable instance counters. Elembic's meta: true selector exists for lower-level metadata queries.

> [!NOTE] Queries inspect the laid-out document
> They need context and can see content later in the document. Avoid making an element's existence depend on a query that counts that same element: Typst may not converge. For a labeled block's line count, use [codly.info](helpers/info.md).

 Set defaults, then customize rendering

Use -set_ for fields such as fill, inset, or numbering. A -show_ callback receives the element, with scoped defaults resolved, and must return content. Use codly.e.fields(it) to read its custom fields; native it.fields() describes Elembic's underlying Typst representation.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

{
  show: codly.number-set_(numbering: "1.")
  show: codly.e.show_(codly.number.with(number: 2), it => {
    text(red, weight: "bold", it)
  })
  codly.new(
    py
    first = 1
    second = 2
    ,
  )
}

// The rules above end with their enclosing scope.
codly.new(
  py
  ordinary = 3
  ,
)


Returning it, or wrapping it as above, preserves the component's existing renderer. Returning fresh content replaces that renderer. For example, codly.lang-show_(it => strong(codly.e.fields(it).body)) displays only the language name and bypasses its usual badge rendering. Constructing a new matching component inside its own show rule can trigger the rule again.

When you need a native show-set rule, use an Elembic selector:

typst
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show codly.e.selector(codly.header): set text(style: "italic")


 Read scoped defaults

codly.e.get reads settings at its position, even without a component instance. codly.e.fields(it) reads the fields of a particular instance, including explicit constructor arguments.

Read resolved fields in show callbacks or query results. A newly constructed instance can still have incomplete fields until Elembic displays it; codly.e.fields(codly.new(...)) is not a way to read all current defaults.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

show: codly.set_(radius: 8pt)
codly.e.get(get => [Current default radius: get(codly.new).radius.])


 Keep custom rules predictable

- Put rules before the content they style, and group related rules in a local { ... } scope or template.
- Target the smallest useful component: a number rule for number formatting, a line rule for rows, a block rule for the whole listing. Prefer existing fields before replacing rendering.
- Keep callbacks free of document-wide queries when fields already contain the needed information. Codly can create many row and number elements.
- Preserve it when adding decoration. Replacing rows or whole blocks can remove the syntax, layout, anchors, and metadata produced by their default renderers.
- Test wrapping, page breaks, and references when a rule changes geometry. Optional diff and syntax features also create internal passes, so an unrestricted query may include supporting elements.

For more detail, see [Elembic show rules](https://pgbiel.github.io/elembic/elements/styling/show-rules.html), [Typst queries](https://typst.app/docs/reference/introspection/query/), and [Codly internals](internals.md).

title: ⚙️ Internals
text:
How Codly works

Codly keeps Typst's syntax highlighting and builds a configurable layout around
it. This guide follows the current implementation from source to output, so you
can choose the right extension point when a theme or field is not enough. For
writing rules and queries, see [Querying and show rules](queries-and-show-rules.md).

 From source to components

[codly.new](components/new.md) is an alias for the block element codly.codly.
It accepts raw content, a source string, or a resolved path. Strings and files
become block raw elements; filenames can supply a language and file badge.
Typst then produces raw.line values containing both plain text and highlighted
content.

mermaid
flowchart TD
    accTitle: From source to a Codly block
    accDescr: Input becomes highlighted lines, optional syntax passes, displayed rows, components, and grid layout with reference metadata.
    Input["Raw content, string, or path"] --> Block["codly.new: prepare source and resolve settings"]
    Block --> Raw["Typst raw: syntax-highlighted raw.line values"]
    Raw --> Passes["Optional diff, rainbow, and sublanguage passes"]
    Passes --> Rows["Select source lines and build displayed rows"]
    Rows --> Parts["Codly components: lines, numbers, badges, highlights, callouts"]
    Parts --> Grid["Grid layout and optional geometry painting"]
    Grid --> Output["Rendered block and reference metadata"]


The components are [Elembic](https://pgbiel.github.io/elembic/) custom elements.
Elembic validates fields, casts shorthand configuration values, and resolves
scoped set/show rules when elements are displayed. That is why
show: codly.number-set_(...) can style numbers generated later by the block
renderer. [Themes](helpers/theme.md) apply these same scoped rules, alongside raw
syntax and text styling.

 Syntax passes reuse Typst

Codly does not implement another language parser. Extra highlighting features
create auxiliary raw blocks and retain their highlighted lines:

- Sublanguages highlight each configured source range with its own language.
  [codly.sublang-block](components/sublang-block.md) stores those lines as
  metadata; the visible row receives the resolved raw.line before its line
  show rule runs.
- Rainbow delimiters use a private classification theme to distinguish code
  from strings and comments, then recolor eligible delimiters in the display
  content. Sublanguage ranges receive their own classification passes.
- Diffs (diff-py or diff,py, for example) create old and new source views
  for each hunk. Removed rows use old-side highlighting; added and context rows
  use new-side highlighting. The final block adds backgrounds and gutters once.

These passes can nest: a diff view can contain sublanguages and rainbow colors.
Auxiliary blocks provide syntax data rather than extra visible listings. They
can still appear in broad element queries, so a count of queried Codly or raw
elements need not equal a count of visible listings.

 Source lines become grid rows

The row builder applies ranges, skips, offsets, and unnumbered-line settings. It
then inserts callout rows and constructs gutter, code, and optional annotation
cells. Annotations can span rows; headers and footers span the columns.

Keep three coordinates separate:

| Coordinate | Used for |
| --- | --- |
| Source line, starting at 1 | Ranges, sublanguages, gutter arrays, callout attachment |
| Displayed number | Number labels and highlight line selection |
| Displayed row index, starting at 0 | Fill palettes and row callbacks, including generated rows |

Here the second source line displays as 102. Its gutter entry and callout use
source coordinates; its highlight uses the displayed number.

typst preview
import "@preview/codly:2.0.0" as codly

codly.new(
  py
  x = 1
  print(x)
  ,
  offset: 100,
  gutters: (auto, ("", "→")),
  highlights: ((line: 102, start: 0, end: 5),),
  callouts: ((line: 2, body: [The second source line.]),),
)


A wrapped line remains one logical code row. Smart indentation formats its
continuations inside that row. Body backgrounds normally come from
[codly.line](components/line.md); whole-line highlights take precedence over
diff backgrounds, which take precedence over the ordinary fill. Header and
footer components own their fills.

 Layout, metadata, and references

For ordinary blocks, Typst lays out the grid directly. Outside gutters, indent
guides, wrap markers, or edge padding use the geometry renderer: metadata marks
cell and page-region boundaries, then painting uses their actual positions.
This lets decorations follow wrapped rows and page breaks without laying out a
second copy of the code.

mermaid
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Layout and metadata support decorations and references
    accDescr: The grid supplies geometry marks for painting, hidden targets for references, and a compact block record for info and continued numbering.
    Grid["Grid and code content"] --> Layout["Typst layout"]
    Layout --> Bounds["Cell and region metadata"]
    Bounds --> Paint["Paint fills, borders, guides, and wrap markers"]
    Grid --> Anchors["Hidden native figure targets"]
    Anchors --> References["Native references via Codly reference components"]
    Grid --> Record["Block record: source count and last number"]
    Record --> Info["codly.info and continued numbering"]


Line, highlight, and annotation references use hidden native figure targets,
while [codly.line-ref](components/line-ref.md) and the other reference
components format the resulting reference text. The enclosing figure label is
discovered automatically; an unlabeled inner figure stops that discovery.

[codly.info](helpers/info.md) reads the compact block record inside context.
Its lines field counts the full source, including omitted lines; last-number
tracks computed numbering. Passing a previous block's label as offset uses
that record to continue numbering.

 Finding an extension point

Start with public fields and themes for layout and appearance. Use component
show rules for a badge, line, highlight, or reference; keep the original element
in your result when you want its existing behavior. Query metadata for document
inspection after layout.

For implementation work, the declarations live in
[codly.typ](https://github.com/Dherse/codly/blob/main/codly.typ), the row and
block pipeline in
[src/lib.typ](https://github.com/Dherse/codly/blob/main/src/lib.typ), and the
position-based painting in
[src/geometry.typ](https://github.com/Dherse/codly/blob/main/src/geometry.typ).
Fields and labels beginning with __ carry internal data and may change; build
customizations on the documented API.
